name: TrueLine: KKL vector-first takeoff engine (geometry measures, QS confirms, rules calculate)
angle: VECTOR-FIRST ENGINE. Every quantity is produced by deterministic geometry code over one internal Sheet Geometry Model (viewports with confirmed scale, pen-weight classes, chained paths, text with direction). A classifier trained from QS corrections decides WHAT a path is; code decides HOW MUCH; a rule pack per contract preamble derives every dependent BQ line; no model-emitted number ever becomes a quantity. Scans are traced by the QS with snapping to a centreline skeleton and logged as labelled data.
thesis:
The digest's spike evidence is unambiguous: on vector input, PyMuPDF, pdf.js and ezdxf reproduce lengths, counts and areas exactly (D1 95.25 m, 8 sumps, 2103.2 m2, all exact; DXF pipe run to 0.003 %), while the best vision models count symbols at 0.40-0.55 accuracy and read dense dimensions at 40-80 %. KKL's inputs are mostly vector PDF from GeBIZ (LTA issues PDF/ZIP only), and the digest's inventory says roughly 60 % of BQ lines (EW-EXCT, EW-BF, EW-DISP, EW-HARD, RC-FW, RC-CONC, asphalt tonnage, kerb haunch) are formulas over four primitives (count, length, area, surface/section volume) plus SDRE/M&W lookups. So the design puts all measurement and calculation in versioned, unit-tested code, and uses learning only for the one step that is genuinely ambiguous on real sheets: which path belongs to which KKL activity code. That step is cheap to get wrong (a misclassified path is visible on screen and corrected in one click) and every correction is a labelled example, whereas a wrong number from a model is invisible until it costs money. This is why the effort curve can fall while money-bearing quantities stay safe: the engine's error sources are enumerable (scale, classification, chaining, rule pack) and each has an on-screen check.

Real LTA-style sheets (PDFill re-save, zero OCGs, all black, pen weights 0.36/0.72/1.08/1.44/2.16 pt, 400-15,000 paths per A3, several scales per page, some pages with text as glyph outlines) dictate how classification must work. First the importer reconstructs viewports from the clip hierarchy (get_drawings(extended=True) 'clip'/'scissor' records) and, where clips are absent, from spatial clustering of path bounding boxes (DBSCAN on bbox centres, gap threshold 3x median path size) with the nearest title text ('DETAIL A', 'SECTION 1-1', 'SCALE 1:20', 'LAYOUT PLAN', 'LONGITUDINAL SECTION'). Each viewport gets a type (layout-plan, long-section, cross-section, detail, schedule, legend, title-block) from text regexes (chainage density 'CH \d+\+\d{3}', 'IL \d+\.\d{2}', 'GL', 'SCALE') plus geometry (long-sections have a horizontal datum line 1.08 pt spanning the viewport with vertical grid ticks; details are small with dimension strings on every side). Scale is resolved per viewport by three independent voters: title text 'SCALE 1:n @ A1/A3' corrected for the actual page size (A1 2384x1684 pt, A3 1191x842 pt), a dimension-line detector (thin 0.36 pt line with 45-degree tick marks or filled triangular arrowheads at both ends, extension lines perpendicular, and a numeric text token whose direction vector is parallel to the line within 5 degrees, giving pt-per-mm votes), and the scale bar. The QS confirms with one click per viewport; the confirmation is stored with the sheet hash and originator template so the same consultant's next sheet is pre-confirmed. The digest's crude voter got 2 of 4 LTA sheets; the dimension-line detector plus per-viewport voting is claim 3 below and is tested on the regression corpus before anything is trusted.

Classification on black-pen sheets keys on features that survive a PDFill re-save: quantised pen weight (0.36 = annotation, dimensions, hatching, leaders; 0.72 = general linework, existing ground; 1.08 = element outlines, cut lines, kerb faces; 1.44/2.16 = borders, formation lines, section cuts), dash pattern (dashed = hidden or existing to be removed; dash-dot = centreline/chainage line; solid = proposed), closure and fill, segment count and curvature, length in metres after scale, the parallel-partner test (a second path of the same weight running parallel at a scaled offset of 0.3-1.5 m for 60 % of its length means a pipe or drain drawn as two walls; offset 0.15-0.30 m means a kerb face and back), hatch membership (>= 20 short parallel strokes at one angle with regular spacing inside a closed loop marks a hatched area whose loop is the measurable polygon; the strokes themselves are 'ignore'), symbol signature (normalised shape hash of small closed paths: square with diagonal, circle with cross, rectangle 600x600 mm scaled, matched against the legend box learned as in extract_pymupdf.py), and label context (nearest text token within 2x text height classified by regex: 'Ø300|300 DIA|RCP' -> DR-PIPE with dia attribute; 'U-DRAIN|UD 600' -> DR-RCU; 'K2A|K2B|KERB' -> RW-KERB; 'SUMP|DIC|MH' -> DR-SUMP; 'RCBC|BOX CULVERT' -> DR-BC; 'ACWC|AC WEARING' -> RW-ACWC; 'GRANITE|CRUSHER RUN|SUB-BASE' -> RW-SUB/RW-BASE; 'FP|FOOTPATH' -> RW-FP). A viewport of type 'detail' or 'cross-section' is never a source of plan lengths or counts; its paths are classified into section roles (existing ground, formation, structure outline, reinforcement) that feed the section-volume kernel instead. The classifier is a per-path feature vector (about 40 features) scored first by rules and legend, then, once corrections exist, by a HistGradientBoosting model (scikit-learn) trained nightly on corrections.jsonl and exported as a compact decision-tree JSON that the single-file app evaluates in the browser; label set = KKL activity codes plus IGNORE, DIMENSION, HATCH, TEXT-OUTLINE, BORDER, EXISTING. Legend learning and originator templates (hash of title-block layout) let the model specialise per consultant without retraining from scratch.

Quantities then come from the measurement kernel, a pure-function library with unit tests and a synthetic DXF-to-PDF round-trip suite (ezdxf drawing add-on PyMuPdfBackend renders known geometry, the PDF path re-measures it). Counts: connected components of a symbol signature outside legend/title/detail viewports, de-duplicated across overlapping viewports, each with its nearest label and chainage. Lengths: Bezier flattening at 0.1 pt tolerance, chaining of same-class segments whose endpoints meet within 0.5 pt, gap bridging across labels when collinear within 2 degrees and the gap is under 3x text height, double-wall runs collapsed to a centreline, length measured over sumps when the rule pack says so, split at chainage ticks so every run carries chainage from/to. Areas: closed loops (or hatch-region loops) with even-odd islands by shoelace, named by contained text, thickness from the rule pack's SDRE road-type lookup so RW-SUB/RW-BASE/RW-ACWC m2 at stated thickness or tonnes fall out. Section-based volumes: in each cross-section viewport the QS confirms which polyline is existing ground and which is formation/structure outline (pre-selected by weight and dash, remembered per template), the kernel computes the end area between them bounded by the section limits, parses the chainage from the viewport title, and integrates between consecutive sections by average end area with the prismoidal correction, reporting both (the digest records AEA over-estimating 5-10 %); long-sections supply GL and IL at every sump so trench depth bands are interpolated exactly as calc_trench.py does today. The rule pack per contract (JSON extracted from the BQ preambles by the existing Extract agent and signed by the chief QS: depth-band edges, working space, bedding, OD table, U-drain outer sizes, nett/no-bulking, rounding) turns primitives into about twenty BQ lines per run in KKL codes, and a chainage ledger (designed quantity per activity code per chainage interval) is exported to SharePoint so monthly SOPA claims and subcon certification become DR Capture chainage lookups rather than fresh measurement.

components.name: Sheet Geometry Model (SGM)
components.role: One JSON schema per sheet (sheet.json, keyed by SHA-256 of the annotation-stripped page): page size/rotation, viewports[{id, clip polygon, type, scale{value, source, confirmed_by, at}}], paths[{id, viewport, items flattened to polylines, width_pt, weight_class, colour, dash, closed, fill, bbox, ocg}], texts[{str, bbox, direction vector, font/outline flag}], images[], and derived layers (chains, symbols, hatch regions). Every quantity cites path ids so any figure can be reconstructed for an SO or subcon dispute.
components.tech: JSON schema in takeoff/schema/sgm.schema.json; Python dataclasses and a matching TypeScript type in the app; gzip'd sheet.json stored next to the PDF on SharePoint
components.build_or_buy: build (about 1 person-week, extends the spike's path dicts)

components.name: PDF importer (server and browser)
components.role: Turns vector PDF into SGM: paths with weight/colour/dash/layer, clip hierarchy for viewports, text with direction vectors, glyph-outline detection (words == 0 with thousands of small Bezier fills routes the page to OCR-on-render). Two routes: PyMuPDF 1.28 get_drawings(extended=True)/get_cdrawings() for batch shadow runs and corpus work (0.85-2.4 s per 120k-segment A1 page per digest), and pdfjs-dist 4.10.38 getOperatorList with a CTM/save/restore/clip stack in the single-file app so drawings never leave the QS's PC. Dual-route agreement within 1 % is one of the confidence checks.
components.tech: takeoff/import_pdf.py (PyMuPDF 1.28.2); takeoff/app/import-pdfjs.js (pdfjs-dist pinned 4.10.38, OPS.constructPath 91, beginMarkedContentProps 70); Poppler pdftocairo -svg as a third independent check on disputed sheets
components.build_or_buy: build (extract_pymupdf.py and extract_pdfjs.mjs already exist; add clip/viewport reconstruction, Bezier flattening, direction vectors: about 3 person-weeks)

components.name: CAD importer (DXF, DWG, LandXML)
components.role: DXF via ezdxf 1.4.4: layers, INSERT block counts, LWPOLYLINE/HATCH lengths and areas, DIMENSION.get_measurement(), $INSUNITS, paper-space VIEWPORT scale; entities are written into the same SGM with layer name as a strong classifier feature and no scale step. DWG converted with LibreDWG dwg2dxf (GPLv3, internal use, not redistributed) on the builder's machine or @mlightcad/libredwg-web 0.7.10 WASM in-browser; ODA File Converter avoided until commercial terms are confirmed. LandXML surfaces (Pnts/Faces) parsed with lxml for exact cut/fill when a client supplies them.
components.tech: takeoff/import_dxf.py (ezdxf), libredwg dwg2dxf CLI, lxml; Civil 3D proxies flagged and the originator asked for Export-to-AutoCAD + LandXML

components.name: Viewport and scale resolver
components.role: Per-viewport scale from three voters: title text 'SCALE 1:n' corrected for page size, dimension-line detector (0.36 pt line with tick/arrow terminators, extension lines, parallel numeric text) giving pt-per-mm votes, and scale-bar length; emits a scale with confidence and a list of 2-3 dimension strings per viewport for the grader. QS confirms with one click; confirmation stored against sheet hash and originator template and reused. Grader blocks export when measured vs printed dimension deviates more than 1 % (green) / 5 % (amber) as the digest's OpenTakeoff-style acceptance test.
components.tech: takeoff/scale.py and app/scale.js (shared test vectors); DBSCAN-style bbox clustering when no clip records exist; regression corpus of real LTA SDRE sheets (kerb 1:20, drain 1:20, mixed 1:25/1:100/1:30)
components.build_or_buy: build (about 2 person-weeks; the digest's heuristic got 2/4 sheets so this is the first thing measured on the corpus)

components.name: Path classifier and legend/template memory
components.role: Assigns each path or symbol a KKL activity code or an ignore class from pen weight, dash, closure/fill, geometry, parallel-partner offset, hatch membership, symbol signature, label regex context and viewport type. v0 = rules + legend learning (as in the spike); v1 = HistGradientBoosting trained on corrections.jsonl, exported to a JSON decision-tree the browser evaluates; per-originator template memory (title-block hash) stores legend maps, confirmed scales and section-role choices. Outputs a per-path class with a calibrated probability used only for routing to review, never for a quantity.
components.tech: takeoff/train_classmap.py (scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier, ~40 features), takeoff/classmap-model.json shipped inside the app, takeoff/legend.py; label set = EW-EXC, EW-EXCT, EW-BF, EW-DISP, EW-HARD, DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, DR-SUMP, DR-BC, RW-KERB, RW-SUB, RW-BASE, RW-ACWC, RW-FP, RC-FW, RC-REB, RC-CONC plus IGNORE/DIMENSION/HATCH/TEXT-OUTLINE/BORDER/EXISTING
components.build_or_buy: build (about 4 person-weeks over months 2-8; no external dataset exists for civil sheets per digest)

components.name: Measurement kernel
components.role: Pure functions over SGM: Bezier flattening, chaining, gap bridging, double-wall centreline collapse, chainage splitting, symbol de-duplication, shoelace areas with islands, hatch-region polygonisation, section end areas with AEA and prismoidal, GL/IL interpolation from long-sections, depth-band bucketing. Emits primitives[{class, unit, qty, path_ids, viewport, chainage_from/to, attributes(dia, size, type), checks{scale_ok, dual_route_ok, legend_ok, label_attached, dimension_grade}}].
components.tech: takeoff/kernel.py and app/kernel.js written to the same spec with shared JSON test vectors; synthetic DXF-to-PDF round-trip suite via ezdxf drawing add-on PyMuPdfBackend; pytest + node:test
components.build_or_buy: build (about 5 person-weeks across the plan; the spike code is the seed)

components.name: Rule packs and calculation layer
components.role: Per-contract JSON rule pack (depth bands e.g. ne 2/2-4/4-6 m or KKL DR bands <1.5/1.5-3/3-6/>6 m, working space per pipe size, bedding/surround, OD table, U-drain outer sizes, kerb unit lengths K2A/K2B 980 mm, pavement thickness by road type from SDRE, nett/no-bulking, concrete rounded up to 0.1 m3, mesh kg/m2 per resolved standard, trench measured over sumps) extracted from the BQ preambles with the existing Extract agent (text only) and signed by the chief QS. calc_trench.py generalised: primitives + rule pack -> BQ lines in KKL codes (EW-EXCT by band, EW-BF, EW-HARD, EW-DISP, RC-FW/RC-CONC/RC-REB for CIS drains and culverts from section area x length, RW-* at thickness or tonnes) plus a chainage ledger.
components.tech: takeoff/calc/*.py and app/calc.js; rulepacks/<contract>.json; bq-map.csv (activity code -> BQ item per client LTA/HDB/PUB/JTC); unit tests per rule
components.build_or_buy: build (about 4 person-weeks; rules replace placeholders in calc_trench.py)

components.name: QS workbench (single-file web app)
components.role: takeoff/index.html on GitHub Pages, same style as DR Capture: pdf.js canvas with an SVG overlay colouring paths by class; viewport list with scale confirm and dimension grader; legend panel; class table with count/length/area, checks and confidence; click-to-relabel (logged); lasso to reassign; 'trace with snap' for scans and for gaps (snaps to vector endpoints, skeleton nodes, and chainage ticks); section tool (pick ground/formation polylines, see end area live); blind-then-reveal mode on a 20 % sample; per-sheet per-class timer with start/pause; seeded known-error items; export CSV rows keyed like DR Capture (activity code, structure type, element, chainage from/to, depth band, size) plus sheet.json and corrections.jsonl to the project SharePoint folder. All geometry work stays in the browser; the Claude API is called only for text (preambles, schedules, legend wording) on projects whose confidentiality tier allows it.
components.tech: single HTML file, pdfjs-dist 4.10.38, inline SVG overlay, IndexedDB for session state, CSV/JSON export via the existing SharePoint CSV path; optional Entra sign-in later
components.build_or_buy: build (about 8 person-weeks across the plan; extends ai/index.html patterns)

components.name: Scan fallback
components.role: Pages with no vector paths or glyph-outline text are rendered at 300 dpi (sub-200 dpi rejected for money-bearing classes per digest), OCR'd locally with PaddleOCR (use_textline_orientation on) for scale text, labels and dimensions, skeletonised (OpenCV thinning) to a centreline graph; the QS traces runs and polygons with snapping to skeleton nodes and edges; symbols are counted by the QS with click-to-count; every trace is stored as (crop, polyline, class) for a later YOLOv8 detector once ~2,000 instances per symbol family exist. Scan-sourced quantities carry source=scan and never graduate past Stage 2 without their own ledger evidence.
components.tech: takeoff/import_raster.py (PyMuPDF render, OpenCV thinning, PaddleOCR); app snapping in JS on a downsampled skeleton
components.build_or_buy: build (extract_raster.py is the seed; about 3 person-weeks in months 7-9)

components.name: Accuracy ledger and graduation dashboard
components.role: ledger.csv (one row per item: sheet hash, viewport, class, source type, stage, engine qty, QS final qty, checks passed, minutes, reviewer, seeded flag) and corrections.jsonl on SharePoint; a second single-file page reads them and shows per class x source: item count, median and p95 error, count exact-match, accept-without-edit rate, confident-wrong count, audit error rate, minutes per sheet, and whether the digest's gate thresholds are met. Rollback triggers computed automatically.
components.tech: takeoff/ledger/index.html (Papa-parse style CSV, no server); weekly export by the Python job

components.name: Ground-truth harvesters
components.role: Two zero-behaviour-change label sources: (a) Bluebeam/Acrobat measurement annotations in QS PDFs on SharePoint read with PyMuPDF (/L, /Vertices, /Measure, /Subj, /BSIColumnData) as in extract_markups.py, paired with the annotation-stripped sheet hash; (b) KKL's historical priced BQs and takeoff workbooks (openpyxl) to seed bq-map.csv. Both feed corrections.jsonl and the ledger.
components.tech: takeoff/harvest_markups.py (PyMuPDF), Microsoft Graph delta query or a folder walk on the synced SharePoint library; openpyxl
components.build_or_buy: build (about 1.5 person-weeks; only if QSs actually use Bluebeam, an open question in the digest)

components.name: Text helpers (Claude API, text tier only)
components.role: Existing ai/index.html Extract agent reads BQ preambles into rule-pack drafts, drain/pipe/sump schedules into size/IL/GL tables, BBS totals for RC-REB, and legend wording; never given drawing pixels on NDA/OSA-tier projects; on open-tier projects it may read a 300 dpi render of a title block or legend as a second opinion on wording, never as a measurer.
components.tech: Claude API via the workbench with page citations and JSON-schema output; confidentiality tier tag per project decides what may be sent

architecture.data_flow: 1) Intake: the QS drops the GeBIZ PDF (or DXF/DWG) into the workbench; the project record carries a confidentiality tier (OSA/NDA = nothing leaves the PC; open = text may go to the Claude API). 2) Import: pdf.js builds sheet.json in the browser (PyMuPDF does the same offline for shadow runs and the corpus); pages with zero words and thousands of tiny fills are flagged 'outline text' and their text layer comes from local OCR on a 300 dpi render; pages with no paths go to the scan fallback. 3) Viewports and scale: clip hierarchy or bbox clustering yields viewports with a type; the resolver proposes a scale per viewport with its voters; the QS confirms; the grader checks 2-3 printed dimensions. 4) Classification: rules + legend + originator template + trained class map give each path a class and probability; the overlay shows it; the QS corrects by click or lasso; corrections append to corrections.jsonl. 5) Measurement: the kernel chains, bridges, collapses double walls, counts symbols, polygonises hatch regions, computes section end areas and interpolates GL/IL; primitives carry path ids, chainage and checks. 6) Calculation: the contract rule pack turns primitives into BQ lines in KKL codes and a chainage ledger; bq-map.csv binds codes to the client's BQ items. 7) Review and export: blind-then-reveal on a 20 % sample, seeded errors, timer; items above the class threshold in Stage 3+ are auto-accepted with a random audit, the rest sit in the review queue; a named QS signs the sheet summary; CSV (DR-keyed rows), sheet.json and ledger rows go to the project SharePoint folder. 8) Learning: a nightly Python job on the builder's PC or a small VM retrains the class map from corrections.jsonl and markup harvests, runs the regression corpus (real sheets + synthetic round trips), refuses to publish a model that regresses, and refreshes the ledger dashboard. 9) Claims and VOs: monthly, DR Capture chainage from/to rows join the chainage ledger to give claimable designed quantities per activity code; VOs diff two revisions' sheet.json (paths added/removed per class) into omission and addition lists.
inputs: Vector PDF drawings from GeBIZ/LTA/HDB/PUB/main contractors (layout plans, long and cross sections, SDRE detail references), often no layers, black pen weights, several scales per sheet
Scanned PDFs (>= 300 dpi accepted for money-bearing classes; below that assist-only)
DXF/DWG when obtainable (MC on MRT subcontracts, client on request); LandXML surfaces when a Civil 3D originator exports them
BQ / Price Document PDFs and their preambles (rule packs), historical priced BQs and takeoff workbooks (bq-map seed)
Drain/pipe/sump schedules and BBS (sizes, IL/GL, rebar totals) via the Extract agent or PyMuPDF text tables
QS corrections, scale confirmations, traces and Bluebeam markups (labels)
DR Capture / DR Verify CSVs on SharePoint (chainage from/to, depth band, activity code) for claim reconciliation
Regression corpus: real KKL/LTA sheets with QS-confirmed quantities plus synthetic DXF-to-PDF round trips
outputs: Takeoff CSV per sheet/tender keyed like DR Capture: activity code, structure type, element, size/dia/type, chainage from/to, depth band, qty, unit, path ids, checks, stage, reviewer
BQ lines per contract (rule pack applied) and a chainage ledger of designed quantities per activity code per interval
sheet.json (SGM) with confirmed scales and class labels; corrections.jsonl; ledger.csv
VO differential lists (omissions from old revision, additions from new) per class
Monthly claim support: DR chainage rows joined to designed quantities with an audit trail per item
Graduation dashboard: per class x source accuracy, automation rate, audited accuracy, minutes per sheet, gate status

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Nothing; the workbench viewer with per-sheet per-class timer and edit log is in use; two-QS agreement measured on ~20 sheets; one-week inbox sample fixes the vector/scan/DXF mix
effort_curve.qs_role: Measurer as today; logs minutes
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Timer data for >= 4 weeks; inter-QS variance per class recorded (digest: this is the accuracy ceiling); format mix known

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Vector PDF/DXF: DR-SUMP/DR-BC counts and schedule reads in Stage 3 (confidence-gated) for repeat originators, Stage 2 elsewhere; DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, RW-KERB lengths in Stage 2 (engine pre-fills, QS verifies every item); derived EW-EXCT/EW-BF/EW-HARD/EW-DISP lines produced by the rule pack on 3 live contracts; CSV export replaces BQ re-typing; scale confirmation per viewport. Areas, sections and scans still manual or assisted tracing.
effort_curve.qs_role: Verifier for counts and linear runs on vector sheets; measurer for areas, volumes, scans; owner of rule packs
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Counts: >= 200 items across >= 5 projects, exact-match >= 98 %, zero confident-wrong (digest Stage 1->2/3 gates). Linear: >= 200 items, median abs error <= 1 %, p95 <= 5 %, dimension grader green on every exported viewport. Effort figure = tender takeoff (35-45 % of QS hours per digest) reduced ~20 % (counts <10 % of tender hours largely removed, trench runs + derived 15-20 % about 40 % faster, BQ entry 15-20 % about 30 % faster), claims and VOs unchanged; verification overhead included

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Vector PDF/DXF: counts in Stage 4 (autonomous with 2-5 % audit); DR-PIPE/DR-RCU/RW-KERB lengths in Stage 3 with the top-80 %-of-value rule still human-checked; RW-ACWC/RW-FP/RW-SUB/RW-BASE areas in Stage 2; CIS RC-CONC/RC-FW from section area x length in Stage 2; section-based EW-EXC end-area volumes in Stage 2 (semi-automatic tool, QS picks polylines); chainage ledger live on >= 10 contracts so drain/kerb/pipe claim lines are DR lookups; VO diff in use; scans traced with snapping (Stage 2).
effort_curve.qs_role: Reviewer and exception handler on vector work; measurer with tools on sections and scans; signs every sheet summary
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Linear to Stage 3: >= 500 verified items, accept-without-edit >= 95 %, escaped-error <= 0.5 %, no money-bearing error in last 300 items, threshold from observed check distribution with auto-accept bucket error <= 0.5 %. Areas to Stage 2: >= 200 items, median error <= 1 % (vector). Effort figure = tender ~40 % faster (x 0.40 share = -16 %), VOs ~30 % faster (x 0.12 = -4 %), claims ~15 % faster via chainage ledger (x 0.27 = -4 %); assumption on shares from the digest's inferred split

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Vector PDF/DXF: counts and linear in Stage 4; areas in Stage 3; section-based volumes and CIS RC build-ups in Stage 3 on vector sections (Stage 2 on scans); LandXML surface volumes exact where supplied; rule packs for all live client templates; class map specialised per originator; scan symbol detector (YOLOv8) in Stage 2 if >= 2,000 instances per family were logged; 15-20 % of items remain human-touched as steady state (digest claims-processing analogue).
effort_curve.qs_role: Estimator, reviewer of exceptions and high-value items, auditor (2-5 % random audit, quarterly blind re-baseline, one fully manual sheet per QS per week)
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Areas to Stage 3: same 500-item gate plus no systematic bias (Togal study showed areas under-measured, so require mean signed error within ±1 %). Volumes to Stage 3: end-area within 5 % of QS figure on >= 80 % of runs across >= 5 contracts and prismoidal vs AEA both reported. Effort figure = tender ~55 % faster (-22 %), VOs ~45 % (-5 %), claims ~25 % (-7 %), ordering/final account ~35 % (-4 %); rollback to Stage 2 on any money-bearing error in the auto-accepted stream

risks.risk: Real sheets are far messier than the synthetic spike: curves, hatching (3,614 green lines on one kerb sheet), overlapping viewports, text breaking lines, rotated pages; classification and chaining accuracy could fall well below the gates
risks.mitigation: Build the 30-sheet real corpus before any promise; measure per-class precision on it in month 2; hatch strokes get their own IGNORE/HATCH class; gap bridging is bounded (collinear within 2 degrees, gap < 3x text height) and every bridge is visible in the overlay; classes that fail the gates stay in Stage 2 with no schedule pressure

risks.risk: Per-viewport scale resolution fails on many sheets (digest: 2 of 4 with the crude voter), and a wrong scale is a systematic money-bearing error
risks.mitigation: Three independent voters plus mandatory QS confirmation per viewport; dimension grader blocks export outside 1 %/5 %; confirmed scales cached per originator template; a plan sheet with no usable dimension strings is flagged and routed to manual scale from a known length

risks.risk: Outline-text pages (SHX exported as geometry) have no readable labels or scale text
risks.mitigation: Automatic detection (words == 0 with thousands of small fills) and local OCR on a 300 dpi render with PaddleOCR; ask originators for PDFSHX=1 or TrueType plots; labels missing means the class is routed to review, never auto-accepted

risks.risk: QS verification time in Stage 2 eats the saving (Togal-style learning-curve effects) so effort does not actually fall
risks.mitigation: Per-sheet timer with start/pause is the only accepted evidence; alternating-sheet A/B inside the same tender; overlay designed for lasso correction of many paths at once; the 6-month figure already includes verification overhead

risks.risk: Automation bias and deskilling: reviewers accept engine values without checking, and lose unassisted skill
risks.mitigation: Blind-then-reveal on a 20 % sample, seeded known-error items with catch rate >= 90 % tracked per QS, one fully manual sheet per QS per week scored against the engine, juniors in reveal-disabled mode for 6 months, reviewer performance measured on catch rate not throughput

key_claims: Claim 1 (input mix, assumption): at least 70 % of the drawing pages KKL's QSs measure at tender arrive as vector PDF with extractable paths (with or without real text); the one-week inbox sample in M0 can refute this, and if vector is under 50 % the effort curve above is not achievable and the scan fallback becomes the main product.

Claim 2 (classification on black-pen sheets): using pen weight, dash, closure/fill, parallel-partner offset, hatch membership, symbol signature and label-regex context, the classifier reaches >= 90 % per-path precision on measurable classes (DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, RW-KERB, DR-SUMP, RW-* areas) after no more than 20 corrected sheets from the same originator template; refuted if the corpus shows precision below 80 % after 20 sheets.

Claim 3 (scale): the three-voter resolver (title text corrected for page size, dimension-line detector, scale bar) proposes the correct scale on >= 80 % of viewports on the real corpus and the QS confirmation takes under 30 s per viewport; refuted if the corpus rate stays near the digest's 2 of 4.

Claim 4 (measurement exactness carries to real sheets): once scale is confirmed and paths are classified, chained lengths and symbol counts from vector geometry are within 1 % / exact of the QS's own re-measurement on >= 95 % of items, as the synthetic spike showed exactly; refuted by a corpus median error above 1 % that is not explained by classification or scale.

Claim 5 (calculation share): >= 60 % of BQ lines in KKL's earthworks and drainage BQs are deterministic functions of the four primitives plus a contract rule pack (digest inference); refuted if reading three live Price Documents shows the share below 40 %.

Claim 6 (verification is cheaper than measuring): the QS's touch time per item in Stage 2 (click/lasso corrections plus checks) is under 30 % of the time to measure the same item by hand, as logged by the timer; refuted if the timer shows Stage 2 sheets taking >= 80 % of baseline minutes after the first 10 sheets.

Claim 7 (section volumes): end-area volumes computed from vector long/cross-section viewports with QS-picked ground and formation polylines are within 5 % of the QS's own figure on >= 80 % of runs; refuted by corpus results outside that band on vector sections (scans excluded).

Claim 8 (confidence proxy): a composite of verifiable checks can be calibrated so that the auto-accepted bucket has an empirical error rate <= 0.5 % per class with an automation rate of >= 60 % for counts and linear items on vector sheets; refuted if achieving 0.5 % requires an automation rate below 30 %, in which case Stage 3 delivers little effort saving.

Claim 9 (inter-QS variance): today's two-QS disagreement per class is at least as large as the engine's error after gates (e.g. >= 1 % on lengths, >= 3 % on areas); if QSs already agree more tightly than the engine can, the gates cannot be passed and the class stays in assist.

Claim 10 (claims join): DR Capture chainage from/to and depth-band rows can be joined to the drawing-derived chainage ledger for drains, pipes and kerbs on most contracts, making monthly claim quantities for those classes a lookup; refuted if site chainage conventions differ from drawing chainages on more than a minority of contracts.

Claim 11 (locality satisfies confidentiality): running all geometry and OCR in the browser or on a KKL machine, with only BQ/preamble/schedule text sent to the Claude API on permitted tiers, satisfies OSA/NDA constraints as read by KKL's contracts person; refuted if a client NDA also forbids any third-party processing of text extracted from the tender documents.

Claim 12 (builder capacity): 42 person-weeks over 24 months fits the builder's part-time allocation (about 0.4 FTE) alongside the existing apps; refuted if the allocation is closer to 0.2 FTE, in which case M6-M8 slip by a year and the 24-month effort figure becomes the 36-month figure.
why_this_wins: It is the only design in which every money-bearing number has a reconstructible provenance (sheet hash, viewport, confirmed scale, path ids, rule pack version) and no probabilistic component ever emits a quantity; the learning is confined to path classification, where a mistake is visible on screen and fixable in one click and every fix is training data. It builds directly on code that already exists and is proven exact (extract_pymupdf.py, extract_pdfjs.mjs, extract_dxf.py, calc_trench.py, extract_markups.py), ships in the single-file GitHub Pages plus SharePoint CSV style the builder already uses, costs about US$250 a month to run with no per-seat SaaS, keeps drawings inside KKL for OSA/NDA tiers, and delivers value early (timer and CSV export in weeks, counts and lengths in shadow by week 18, rule-pack BQ lines by week 24) while the digest's five-stage per-class gates decide, on KKL's own ledger data rather than a vendor's claim, when each activity code moves from assist to autonomous-with-audit.

name: Shadow Ledger — capture-first takeoff flywheel for KKL
angle: CAPTURE-FIRST (data flywheel): ship zero-behaviour-change capture of the QSs' existing takeoffs (PDF measurement annotations, Excel BQ workbooks, DR Capture rows) before any engine, run the engine in blind shadow against every captured sheet, and graduate item classes only on ledger evidence.
thesis:
KKL has no external truth to train or test a takeoff engine against: Singapore has no civil SMM, no public civil drawing dataset exists, and vendor accuracy claims are unaudited (digest, topics 3 and 7). The only benchmark that exists is the takeoff a KKL QS finishes every working day, and most of it is already machine-readable with no change to how they work: a measurement drawn in Bluebeam Revu, Acrobat, Foxit or PDF-XChange is stored inside the saved PDF as a standard annotation (Line /L, PolyLine and Polygon /Vertices, Count) with an ISO 32000 /Measure scale, a /Subj subject, a layer, an author and a date, and PyMuPDF reads all of it (digest topic 4; spike extract_markups.py recovered 52.92 m, 134.06 m and 2103.2 m2 with subject and author exactly). The QS's BQ workbook already holds the item-to-quantity mapping (openpyxl), and DR Capture already records claim-side quantities per activity code with struct, method, IW x depth, chainage, depth band, soil type, spoil destination and loads (index.html CSVHEAD). So the first deliverable is not an engine but a Ledger: a nightly job on an office PC that walks the OneDrive-synced tender and claims libraries, fingerprints every sheet, pulls every measurement annotation, maps its subject to a KKL activity code, harvests the workbook and the DR rows, and appends one JSONL record per measurement. From week 6 KKL owns a growing corpus of (sheet, region geometry, scale, activity code, quantity, QS, minutes) pairs at zero licence cost, and the effort baseline that criterion 1 demands comes from annotation timestamps rather than self-report.

The engine (the PyMuPDF/pdf.js/ezdxf spikes, extended to real sheets: per-viewport scale, pen-weight signatures, legend learning, label attachment, exclusion zones) then runs in shadow on every sheet that carries QS markups. The shadow scorer matches engine items to QS markups by class and geometric overlap (shapely), scores per class x source (DXF, vector PDF with text, vector PDF with outline text, scan >= 300 dpi), and files every disagreement with a reason code. Disagreements are the product in the first six months: the weekly scorecard shows the chief QS where the engine and the QS differ, which surfaces QS omissions and double counts before a bid goes in (a second pair of eyes with no automation risk), and tells the part-time builder which failure mode to fix next. Each QS correction of the engine, and each engine finding the chief QS confirms against the QS, becomes a labelled example, a row in the per-template signature-to-code table that is the engine's classifier, and a regression case that must pass before any engine release.

Graduation is per class x source, using the digest's five-stage framework with its thresholds verbatim: Stage 1 shadow needs >= 200 items or >= 30 sheets across >= 5 projects and >= 2 sources, median absolute error <= 1 % (vector/DXF) or <= 3 % (scan), p95 <= 5 %, count exact-match >= 98 %, zero confident-wrong items and a checked calibration; Stage 2 assist needs >= 500 verified items, accept-without-edit >= 95 %, escaped-error <= 0.5 % and no money-bearing error in the last 300; Stage 3 confidence-gates auto-acceptance with a 10 % -> 5 % -> 2 % random audit and a top-80 %-of-value always-check rule; Stage 4 is autonomous with audit and a named QS still signs. Because the measurement code emits no probability, confidence is a composite of verifiable checks (scale cross-check, dual-route agreement, unambiguous signature mapping, label attachment, template familiarity, topology) whose empirical error rate per check pattern is calibrated on the shadow data itself, and any missing check is sub-threshold. Assist mode is also capture-first: the engine writes its proposals as measurement annotations on a KKL-ENGINE layer of a copy of the PDF, the QS reviews in the tool they already use, and the nightly diff between engine annotations and final annotations is the corrections log. Money stays safe because nothing auto-accepts until the ledger proves it, derived money lines (EW-EXCT, EW-BF, EW-DISP, EW-HARD, RC-CONC) are unit-tested calculator code over graduated primitives and a per-contract preamble rule set, and every quantity carries an audit trail (sheet fingerprint, path ids, scale source, legend match, checks passed, QS who signed) that can be reconstructed for an SO, a main contractor or an adjudicator.

components.name: Calculator and contract rule sets
components.role: Turns graduated primitives into BQ lines as versioned, unit-tested code: trench excavation by depth band from run length x trench width (OD + working space per preamble) x depth from GL/IL interpolated between sumps, bedding/surround (EW-HARD), backfill (EW-BF), disposal (EW-DISP = excavation less backfill, nett, no bulking), kerb haunch, pavement layers from area x SDRE thickness by road type (RW-SUB, RW-BASE, RW-ACBC, RW-ACWC), CIS drain/culvert/sump concrete, formwork and rebar from length x SDRE section lookup or BBS read (RC-CONC, RC-FW, RC-REB), concrete rounded up to 0.1 m3, fabric nett. Rules live in rules/<contract>.json (depth-band edges e.g. n.e. 2/2-4/4-6 m or 0.25 m stages, working space per pipe size, band-by-invert vs band-by-max-depth, trench measured over sumps, disposal in m3 or tonnes) extracted from the tender's General and Particular Preambles by Claude Extract (text-only pages) and confirmed by the chief QS per tender.
components.tech: Python (generalise takeoff/calc_trench.py), pytest, JSON rule sets, SDRE/M&W lookup tables in reference/ (DRA/KER/PAV sheets, mesh kg/m2 resolved to standard)

components.name: Shadow scorer
components.role: For every sheet with QS markups, runs the engine (blind, results not shown) and matches engine items to markups: linear by buffered-overlap fraction (buffer 3 pt), areas by IoU >= 0.8, counts by point-in-symbol-bbox; records per pair the signed error, and per class x source the sheet-total error, item median absolute error, p95, recall (QS items the engine found), precision (engine items with no QS counterpart), count exact-match, confident-wrong count (score above proposed threshold with error > 10 %), and mean signed error (to catch the systematic under-measurement of areas reported for Togal). Truth is 'QS final after chief-QS review of disagreements' and the workbook figure, not the raw markup, with the two-QS baseline disagreement as the accuracy ceiling.
components.tech: Python, shapely 2.0, DuckDB; outputs capture/ledger/shadow_scores.csv

components.name: Confidence proxy and calibration
components.role: Per-item score for deterministic geometry built from checks: C1 scale confirmed (title-block scale agrees with scale bar or >= 2 dimension strings within 0.5 %); C2 item inside a single viewport with confirmed scale; C3 dual-route agreement (PyMuPDF vs pdf.js, or vector vs 300 dpi raster) within 1 %; C4 signature-to-code mapping unambiguous (top mapping >= 0.95 with >= 20 examples in that template family); C5 label attached within threshold and consistent with schedule; C6 template family has >= 30 shadow-scored sheets; C7 topology (run ends at sump/junction, polygon closed, no duplicate overlap); C8 exclusion zones applied; C9 for scans, dpi >= 300 and OCR word confidence >= 0.9. Composite is not a weighted sum: it is the check pattern, and the auto-accept bucket is the set of patterns whose empirical error rate on shadow data is <= 0.5 % with >= 200 items. Missing check = sub-threshold. Calibration table and reliability curve recomputed monthly per class.
components.tech: Python, pandas; calibration table capture/ledger/calibration.csv

components.name: Assist writer and corrections diff
components.role: Stage 2+: writes engine proposals as measurement annotations on a KKL-ENGINE optional-content layer of a copy of the sheet, subject = activity code, custom columns = score, checks passed, engine version, path ids. The QS reviews in Bluebeam or Takeoff Pad: keep = accept, move vertices = edit, delete = spurious, draw new = missed. The nightly Ledger diff between engine annotations and the QS's final annotations yields corrections with reason codes (wrong class, wrong scale/viewport, missed, spurious, wrong band, legend decoy, label mismatch, duplicate). On a 20 % sample of sheets the engine layer is withheld until the QS's own markups are captured (blind-then-reveal, cognitive forcing per digest).
components.tech: PyMuPDF add_polyline_annot/add_polygon_annot + xref_set_key for /Measure, /IT, /OC; same extractor for diff

components.name: Regression corpus and runner
components.role: Every correction and every chief-QS-confirmed engine finding becomes a case: regress/<sheet_id>.json (fingerprint, expected items, tolerance). Real sheets are confidential, so the corpus lives in the SharePoint Takeoff Ledger library and engine/regress.py runs locally before any engine, library, prompt or rule-set change (any regression sends the class back to shadow for 100 items). Only synthetic sheets (make_sample_drawing.py round trips, ezdxf-to-PDF with known quantities) run in GitHub Actions.
components.tech: Python, pytest, DuckDB; GitHub Actions for synthetic set only

components.name: Scorecard, class status and sign-off pages
components.role: Three single-file pages in DR Verify style that load CSVs from the synced Ledger folder (no server, no public data): scorecard.html (weekly engine-vs-QS disagreements per sheet with page render and reason code, chief QS adjudicates), status.html (per class x source: stage, N items, median/p95/bias, accept-without-edit, audit accuracy, escaped errors, automation rate, calibration curve, minutes per sheet per class, QS minutes per S$1m measured), signoff.html (per bid/claim: auto-accepted items with checks, review queue, top-80 %-of-value list, named QS initials before export, seeded known-error catch rate).
components.tech: HTML/JS single files on GitHub Pages; PapaParse; pdf.js 4.10.38 for page render

components.name: Claims roll-up
components.role: Monthly SOPA claim and subcon-certification quantities from captured site data rather than re-measurement: DR rows rolled up per activity code x zone x chainage x depth band x soil type under the contract rule set, joined to the BQ item library, reconciled to tickets/DOs/weighbridge (loads x capacity x 1/bulking vs surveyed bank volume with the residual as a KPI), and compared in shadow to the QS's actual claim pack for that month; produces a draft claim pack CSV and provisional-quantity admeasurement tracker. ~30 claim packs a month (digest inference) make this the largest recurring effort pool.
components.tech: Python, pandas, DuckDB; rules/<contract>.json shared with the calculator; CSV to SharePoint

components.name: Volumes engine

Inputs LandXML (lxml Pnts/Faces), DXF 3DFACE/contours (ezdxf), drone DSM/LAS (PDAL), vector-PDF contours with elevation labels (assist only, explicit accuracy penalty). Validated against Civil 3D/Propeller volumes on one real project before first use in a claim.

architecture.data_flow: 1. INTAKE: contracts tags each project with a confidentiality tier (T0 public/own, T1 client-confidential text OK, T2 NDA/OSA nothing leaves KKL) in a project register CSV; QSs keep saving marked-up PDFs and BQ workbooks to the agreed SharePoint folders as today; DR Capture CSVs keep flowing to Site Logs. 2. CAPTURE (nightly, office PC): Ledger job fingerprints each new/changed sheet, extracts markups, maps subjects to codes, harvests workbooks and DR rows, computes minutes per sheet per class from annotation timestamps, appends JSONL and writes daily CSV rollups to the Takeoff Ledger library. 3. SHADOW (nightly): geometry engine runs on every captured sheet the QS measured (locally; DXF fast path when present); shadow scorer pairs engine items with markups and workbook figures, writes shadow_scores.csv and disagreements with reason codes; calibration table updated. 4. WEEKLY LOOP (1 h chief QS + builder): scorecard.html shows disagreements; chief QS adjudicates each (QS right / engine right / both wrong / rule question); adjudications become labels, signature-table rows and regression cases; the top reason code of the week is the builder's next task; status.html shows each class x source against its gate. 5. ASSIST (per class once Stage 1 gate passes): engine writes proposals as a KKL-ENGINE annotation layer on a copy of the sheet; QS reviews in Bluebeam/Takeoff Pad; nightly diff yields corrections; calculator emits derived BQ lines into a quantities CSV with per-line audit trail that the QS pastes or links into the BQ workbook. 6. GATED (per class once Stage 2 gate passes): items whose check pattern is in the calibrated auto-accept bucket are locked with their score; sub-threshold items, the top-80 %-of-value items, a 10 % (later 5 %, 2 %) random audit sample and seeded known-error items go to the QS review queue in signoff.html; a named QS initials the bid/claim summary before export; rollback triggers (any money-bearing error in the auto stream, audit error rate > 2x baseline, new template family until 50 clean items, any engine/rule change failing regression) demote the class automatically in status.html. 7. CLAIMS (monthly): claims roll-up drafts each contract's SOPA claim pack from DR rows, tickets and (where flown) drone surface differences under rules/<contract>.json, shadowed against the QS's own pack until its gate passes, then assist, then gated. 8. WHAT THE QS SEES: Stage 0-1 nothing new except a tool chest and a weekly note listing sheets where the engine found a possible omission or double count; Stage 2 a pre-marked engine layer on their sheet and an 'engine qty' column beside theirs in the workbook, with 20 % of sheets arriving blind; Stage 3 locked auto-accepted items with a score, a shorter review queue, the value list, and a sign-off page; Stage 4 an exceptions queue, the audit sample, one fully manual sheet per QS per week scored against the engine, and the monthly status board. 9. AUDIT TRAIL: every quantity exported carries sheet_id, page, viewport scale source, path ids, legend match, checks passed, engine version, rule-set version, QS initials, so any figure can be rebuilt for an SO, MC or adjudicator.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Nothing yet. Ledger captures markups, workbooks and DR rows; minutes per sheet per class derived from annotation timestamps; two-QS blind baseline on ~20 sheets gives the inter-QS disagreement ceiling per class.
effort_curve.qs_role: Unchanged: measurer in Bluebeam/Excel; chief QS spends ~1 h/week on the scorecard.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Ledger holds >= 100 markups from >= 3 projects; week-1 inbox sample shows the vector/outline/scan/DXF mix and whether >= 50 % of sheets carry annotations (else Takeoff Pad is built first); money-bearing error defined and signed (larger of 2 % of item value or S$2,000 claims/subcon, S$10,000 tender line, per digest).

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Counts and schedule reads (DR-SUMP, DR-SCUP, DR-CONN nr; pipe/sump/drain schedules, BBS totals) at Stage 2-3 on vector PDF and DXF; DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, RW-KERB lengths at Stage 2 assist; derived EW-EXCT/EW-HARD/EW-BF/EW-DISP lines produced by the calculator under confirmed rule sets at Stage 2; BQ workbook harvest and engine-quantity column reduce BQ entry; claims roll-up at Stage 2 on 5 contracts; shadow diff catches omissions before bid.
effort_curve.qs_role: Measurer with pre-filled counts and pre-marked drain/kerb runs to verify; 20 % of sheets blind; reviewer of claim roll-up drafts on pilot contracts.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Counts passed Stage 1 gate (>= 200 items, >= 5 projects, exact-match >= 98 %, zero confident-wrong) and are into Stage 3 on vector PDF; linear classes passed Stage 1 (median <= 1 %, p95 <= 5 %); estimate uses digest hour shares (counts < 10 % and BQ entry 15-20 % of tender hours, tender 35-45 % of QS hours, claims 25-30 %) so ~10 points saved is an inference to be replaced by ledger minutes.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Counts at Stage 4; DR-PIPE/DR-RCU/RW-KERB at Stage 3 (confidence-gated, 5 % audit) on vector PDF and DXF; derived trench lines auto once primitives and level reads (IL/GL from long section or schedule, >= 98 % exact) pass; RW-ACWC/RW-FP/RW-SUB/RW-BASE areas at Stage 2-3 with SDRE thickness lookup; RC-CONC/RC-FW build-ups for CIS drains and sumps at Stage 2; claims roll-up at Stage 3 on ~20 contracts; VO differential (revision diff of vector geometry and schedules) at Stage 2; bulk EW-EXC from LandXML/DXF/drone surfaces at Stage 1-2 on projects that have surfaces.
effort_curve.qs_role: Reviewer and exception handler on graduated classes; measurer on areas, RC and volumes; signs every bid and claim; one manual sheet per week for skill maintenance.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Linear classes passed Stage 2 gate (>= 500 verified items, accept-without-edit >= 95 %, escaped-error <= 0.5 %, no money-bearing error in last 300) and calibration shows auto-accept bucket error <= 0.5 %; areas passed Stage 1 with |mean signed error| <= 0.5 % (guard against systematic under-measurement); claims roll-up within 2 % of the QS pack for 3 consecutive months on >= 5 contracts; effort proven by alternating-sheet A/B within projects, not self-report.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Counts, linear and area classes at Stage 4 (2-5 % audit) on vector PDF and DXF; derived earthworks and pavement lines fully calculator-driven; RC-CONC/RC-FW at Stage 3, RC-REB at Stage 3 only where a BBS is issued; EW-EXC from surfaces at Stage 3 on surface-input projects, PDF contour route stays Stage 2; claims roll-up at Stage 4 on all ~30 contracts with drone surface differences where flown; VO diff at Stage 3; scans >= 300 dpi at Stage 2 with YOLO-assisted sump counts; soil-class disposal split and under-strut staging remain assisted.
effort_curve.qs_role: Estimator, reviewer of last resort, exception handler and signatory; measurement by hand only on scans, contours and judgement items; roughly 15-20 % of items still human-touched even in graduated classes (claims-processing steady state per digest).
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Each Stage 4 class has 12+ months at Stage 3 with audit accuracy >= 99.5 % and zero rollbacks in the last 2 quarters; quarterly blind re-baseline shows QS unassisted skill within 5 % of baseline; volumes engine validated against Civil 3D/Propeller on one real project before first claim use; 45 points saved is an inference stacked on digest hour shares and must be read off the ledger.

Tender department to request DXF/DWG and LandXML surfaces from clients and main contractors on every job (removes scale and classification error sources)
Agreement in writing on the money-bearing error definition, the accuracy definition (item vs sheet vs value-weighted) and the per-class tolerances before Stage 1
Management commitment that time saved becomes tender capacity in year one, and that reviewers are measured on catch rate, not sheets per day

risks.mitigation: Week-1 inbox sample decides; if < 50 % of sheets annotated, ship Takeoff Pad first (writes standard annotations so the same Ledger reads them) and still harvest workbooks and DR rows; shadow starts on whatever is captured

risks.risk: Markup hygiene: subjects are free text, layers inconsistent, per-viewport scales missing, so labels are noisy
risks.mitigation: Tool chest with KKL codes, subject_map.csv with fuzzy match, Claude classification of subject strings, weekly chief-QS confirmation; unmapped markups excluded from gates but kept for later

risks.risk: QS markups are not truth (omissions, double counts, stale vs workbook); engine judged against wrong answers
risks.mitigation: Truth = QS final after chief-QS adjudication of disagreements plus the workbook figure; two-QS baseline gives the disagreement ceiling; escaped errors found by SO/MC feed back as labels

risks.risk: Real sheets are far harder than the synthetic spike (multi-viewport, no layers, outline text, hatching, rotated pages) and engine accuracy stalls below gates
risks.mitigation: Per-template-family tables and gates keep the class in shadow until evidence exists; viewport scale confirmed by QS and stored; outline-text pages routed to OCR; DXF requested to bypass the problem; no promise of automation until the ledger shows it

risks.risk: Real Bluebeam annotation keys (/VP viewport scales, Count markups, /BSIColumnData) differ from the synthetic spike
risks.mitigation: Verify on one real KKL PDF in week 2 with both PyMuPDF and pypdf; fall back to Bluebeam Markups List CSV export for values while geometry parsing is fixed

risks.risk: Part-time builder bandwidth; project stalls after capture
risks.mitigation: Strict milestone order with capture first (value without engine), reason-code-driven backlog so each week has one concrete fix, single-file conventions already used, runbook and corpus in SharePoint so work survives the builder

risks.risk: Confidentiality breach by sending NDA/OSA drawings to a cloud model
risks.mitigation: All geometry extraction, measurement, OCR and detector training run on KKL machines; only text/table pages of tier T0/T1 projects reach the Claude API; tier enforced in the Ledger job and workbench; audit log of what was sent

risks.risk: Automation bias and deskilling once assist and gating are on
risks.mitigation: Blind-then-reveal on 20 % of sheets, seeded known-error items with catch-rate target >= 90 %, one fully manual sheet per QS per week scored against the engine, juniors in reveal-disabled mode for 6 months, quarterly blind re-baseline

risks.risk: Effort reduction fails to materialise because the top-80 %-of-value rule keeps most money under human check
risks.mitigation: Measure it: ledger minutes and A/B assignment; relax the value rule per class after two clean audit windows; put early effort into the recurring claims roll-up where ~30 packs a month sit

risks.risk: SharePoint sync conflicts or file locks corrupt the ledger or a QS's working PDF
risks.mitigation: Ledger is append-only JSONL written by one job; engine never edits the QS's file, it writes a copy with the KKL-ENGINE layer; DuckDB local working store; nightly batch outside working hours

risks.risk: New consultant template or client causes silent drift in gated classes
risks.mitigation: Operational-design-domain rule: any new template family or source routes all items to review until 50 clean items; monthly PSI on check-pattern distribution acted on only with an audit accuracy drop; regression run before every release

risks.risk: Volumes and disposal split cannot be measured from PDFs and remain the biggest money lines
risks.mitigation: Treat as surface problems: baseline survey, LandXML/DXF from designers, drone RTK surfaces agreed jointly with the MC; PDF contour route stays assist-only with an explicit accuracy penalty; disposal split stays assisted with SI citations

key_claims: At least half of the sheets KKL QSs measure at tender are saved as PDFs carrying measurement annotations (Bluebeam/Acrobat/Foxit/PDF-XChange) in a SharePoint or synced folder; refute by the week-1 inbox sample showing < 50 % (then Takeoff Pad must precede shadow).

PyMuPDF (with pypdf as fallback) recovers geometry, /Measure or /VP scale, subject, author, date and value from real Revu Line/PolyLine/Polygon/Count annotations to within 0.1 % of Bluebeam's own value; verified only on a synthetic file so far (spike extract_markups.py); refute on one real KKL PDF.
Vector PDF (with or without real text) is >= 60 % of incoming tender sheets, so the deterministic engine covers most money-bearing primitives; refute by the inbox sample (digest lists this as open).

A per-template-family signature-to-code table learned from markup overlaps reaches >= 95 % top-1 classification on new sheets from the same consultant after ~20 sheets, on layer-less all-black LTA-style drawings; assumption, refute with shadow precision/recall.

Per-item confidence built from deterministic checks (scale cross-check, dual-route agreement, unambiguous mapping, label attachment, template familiarity, topology) can be calibrated so the auto-accept bucket's empirical error is <= 0.5 % with >= 200 items per class; the digest marks this untested.
Annotation timestamps (/M, /CreationDate) give a usable per-sheet, per-class effort baseline without a timer; assumption, refute if Revu writes dates without time or only at save.

Inter-QS disagreement on KKL sheets is within ~2 % on lengths and ~3 % on areas (SG norms in digest), so the 1 %/3 %/5 % gates are meaningful; refute with the two-QS baseline; if larger, gates must use the measured ceiling.

About 60 % of BQ lines (trench excavation, backfill, disposal, bedding, lean, formwork, concrete, asphalt tonnage, kerb haunch) are formulas over graduated primitives and preamble lookups, so graduating primitives graduates most lines (digest inference); refute by mapping 3 live BQs line by line.
Shadow disagreements surface at least one real QS omission or double count per 10 sheets in the first 3 months, giving value before any automation; assumption, refute from the scorecard log.

Contract preambles can be extracted into machine-checkable rule sets from text pages by the Claude workbench without breaching confidentiality tiers, and chief-QS confirmation takes under an hour per tender; assumption on tiers and effort.

The claims roll-up from DR rows, tickets and surfaces matches the QS's certified monthly pack within 2 % on most contracts once rule sets are right, making ~30 packs a month the largest early effort saving (digest hour shares); refute with 3 months of shadow on 5 contracts.

Steady state leaves 15-20 % of items human-touched even in graduated classes (claims-processing benchmark in digest), so a 55 % effort floor at 24 months is realistic rather than pessimistic; refute if audit and value rules force a higher touch rate.
why_this_wins: With one part-time builder, no external civil dataset and no Singapore civil SMM, the only scalable source of truth is what KKL's QSs already produce every day, and it is free to capture: the spike already proved the markup extractor, the BQ workbooks and DR Capture rows already exist, and the nightly job needs no licence and no change to how anyone works. Every other angle must build an engine first and then find a way to test it; this angle tests the engine against real KKL sheets from the first week it runs, so accuracy, effort baseline and the audit trail all come from the same ledger and no class is promised until the evidence is in the status board. It delivers value early without automation risk (shadow disagreements catch QS errors before bids; the claims roll-up drafts ~30 packs a month), keeps money safe by construction (nothing auto-accepts without a calibrated check pattern, derived lines are tested code over graduated primitives, a named QS signs, rollback is automatic), respects confidentiality (all geometry stays on KKL machines, only tiered text reaches the model), and fits the stack exactly (Python job on an office PC, CSV/JSONL to SharePoint, single-file pages on GitHub Pages, the existing Claude workbench for text). The flywheel also compounds: each correction is a label, a classifier row and a regression case, so the engine gets better in proportion to the work the QSs were already doing.

name: Surface Ledger: survey-first progress measurement, tender second
angle: SURVEY-FIRST FOR PROGRESS. Treat the monthly SOPA claim on ~30 contracts, subcontractor certification and MC back-charges as a reconciliation problem over data KKL already produces (DR Capture rows, survey surfaces, tickets, delivery orders), not a drawing-understanding problem. Bulk volumes come from surface differencing; linear/count/area items from DR chainage rows cross-checked against deliveries; disposal from staging-ground tonnage by stream. Everything rolls up through one per-contract BQ item map with an audit trail fit for SOP Act claims and joint measurement. Tender takeoff plugs into the same item map and calculator later.
thesis:
The digest's own inventory says monthly progress claims plus subcontractor certification take an estimated 25-30% of KKL QS hours (topic 2, inference, low confidence), recur on a fixed cadence on ~30 live public-sector contracts (~30 claim packs a month plus subcon certifications), and are 'data-pipeline and reconciliation problems, not drawing-measurement problems' that 'may free more QS hours sooner than tender automation'. Unlike tender takeoff, every claim quantity gets independent ground truth within weeks: the Superintending Officer's certification, the main contractor's joint measurement, the subcontractor's acceptance. That makes claims the fastest place to build the per-class accuracy ledger the graduation framework (topic 5) needs, and it needs no scale detection, no legend learning and no OCR of drawings to deliver first value.

The design has four engines and one map. (1) A surface engine, Python and open libraries only, running on a KKL machine: LandXML (lxml Pnts/Faces), LAS/LAZ (PDAL or laspy), DXF 3DFACE/contours (ezdxf) go to a TIN (scipy.spatial.Delaunay) and a 0.25 m 2.5D grid; volumes are per-cell height differences clipped to zone polygons (shapely), the CloudCompare 2.5D method the digest rates most accurate against average-end-area's 5-10% over-estimate (topic 6). Bulk excavation EW-EXC, under-strut EW-EXCTD and fill EW-BF become surface_A minus surface_B under the contract's preamble rule, with both surface hashes in the audit row. (2) A DR reconciliation engine: DR Capture already records activity_code, zone, ch_from_m, ch_to_m, depth_band, soil_type, spoil_to, loads_10w, loads_12w, loads_out, qty, unit, machines, machine_hours (index.html CSVHEAD). Loads x nominal capacity / (1+bulking[soil_type]) gives an implied bank m3 per zone per period; the residual against the surveyed bank m3 is a KPI (digest: persistent gap >10% flags under-filled trucks, ticket leakage or misclassified material), and it calibrates KKL-specific bulking, m3/load and m3/h that feed tender rates. Linear items (DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, DR-BC, RW-KERB) are sum(ch_to - ch_from) per spec cross-checked against precast delivery notes (unit count x 1.0 m or 0.5 m per LTA SDRE); counts (DR-SUMP) against delivery notes; asphalt (RW-ACWC/RW-ACBC) against weighbridge tonnes because LTA M&W pays asphalt by weight; RC-CONC against concrete DOs; RC-REB against rebar delivery notes / BBS; EW-DISP against staging-ground tonnage by stream (Good Earth S$1.20/t, Soft Clay S$5.00/t, topic 6). (3) A claim-pack generator (single-file web app on GitHub Pages, SheetJS export) that turns those reconciled quantities into this-period and cumulative BQ item quantities against provisional quantities, a PSSCOC/SOP Act payment claim schedule, a back-to-back subcon certificate, and an audit appendix listing every DR row id, ticket id and surface hash behind each line. (4) A joint-measurement workflow that makes the fortnightly surface the shared record with the main contractor's surveyor. The map is bq_map.csv per contract: BQ item number <-> activity code + struct + spec_element + depth_band + unit + preamble rule (nett vs bulked, band edges, measured over sumps, survey-paid vs design-nett), built once per contract by the QS with the existing Claude Extract agent on the Price Schedule PDF.

Money stays safe because every quantity in a claim has two independent sources (survey vs loads; DR chainage vs deliveries; tonnage vs volume) and the pack is generated only where they agree within the class tolerance; disagreements go to the QS queue with both numbers shown. The graduation framework is applied per activity code per contract using SO-certified quantities as the truth signal: shadow (engine runs beside the QS's manual pack), assist (engine drafts, QS verifies every line), confidence-gated (lines auto-accepted where the two-source agreement, DR Verify status and stage history clear the threshold, top-80%-of-value lines always human-checked, 10% random audit decaying to 2-5%), autonomous-with-audit. A named QS signs every claim throughout; the engine never signs.

Tender comes second and reuses the same parts: bq_map for the new price schedule, the calc layer (calc_trench.py generalised with per-contract preamble rules), the surface engine for cut/fill when LandXML/DXF surfaces are supplied, and the vector-PDF/DXF primitive extractors already proven in the spikes. Because the claims ledger will by then hold KKL's own bulking factors, m3/load and machine productivities, tender rates improve too. QS effort falls first on the recurring work, and it falls on all ~30 contracts at once as DR data coverage grows, not one tender at a time.

components.name: Surface engine (takeoff/surface/)
components.role: Read baseline, design and periodic as-built surfaces; build TIN and 0.25 m grid; compute cut/fill per zone polygon and per depth band; emit volumes CSV with surface hashes and engine version. Files: landxml.py (lxml Pnts/Faces), las_grid.py (PDAL pipeline JSON, laspy fallback), dxf_surface.py (ezdxf 3DFACE / contour polylines with Z), tin.py (scipy.spatial.Delaunay), volume.py (numpy per-cell difference, CloudCompare 2.5D style, 10 cm noise threshold), zones.py (shapely clip to zone/claim-area polygons and exclusion masks for machines, stockpiles, water). Validated against the drone vendor's own volume report and against synthetic surfaces with analytic volumes before first claim use.
components.tech: Python 3.12, lxml, PDAL (or laspy), ezdxf 1.4, scipy, numpy, shapely; runs on a KKL office PC, no cloud (surfaces of client sites never leave KKL)
components.build_or_buy: build (about 600 lines; digest topic 6 lists exactly these libraries)

components.name: Survey intake
components.role: Baseline surface = the pre-construction level survey LTA M&W Ch.3 already requires; fortnightly RTK drone flights (weekly on fast bulk sites) delivering LAS/LAZ + DEM GeoTIFF + ortho; total-station strut-level surveys (CSV points) for decked/under-strut EW-EXCTD areas where drones cannot see; design surfaces requested as LandXML from the client/MC (Civil 3D surfaces do not survive DXF, digest topic 1). components.name: DR reconciliation engine (claims/index.html, tab 'Reconcile')

Per contract, zone, period and activity code: implied bank m3 = (loads_10w x cap_10w + loads_12w x cap_12w) / (1 + bulking[soil_type]); residual vs surveyed bank m3 shown as KPI; bulking, m3/load per truck class and m3/machine-hour per excavator class calibrated from the residual. Confidence-gated (Stage 3) for DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, DR-SUMP, RW-KERB, EW-DISP (tickets), RW-ACWC (weighbridge) where two sources agree within tolerance; EW-EXC/EW-BF confidence-gated on sites with >=3 signed JM cycles within 3%; RC-CONC, RC-REB, RC-FW, RW-SUB/BASE/FP in assist. effort_curve.what_is_automated: Claims autonomous-with-audit (Stage 4, 2-5% audit) for linear, count, ticket and survey-volume classes on all covered contracts; RC classes confidence-gated; JM packs routine with MCs that accept shared surfaces; in-house drone pilot option in place. Tender: counts and schedule reads confidence-gated on vector PDF/DXF; lengths (DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, RW-KERB) confidence-gated on DXF and clean vector PDF; areas and level-based volumes in assist; VO differential takeoff in assist. KKL-calibrated bulking, m3/load and m3/h feed tender rates.

Claims effort down ~70% on all contracts (~19% of total) + tender counts/linear/calc gated (~10%) + VO (~3%) + ordering/final account (~3%). Proven by logged minutes with alternating-month A/B on the same contract, not self-report.
