risks.risk: CAAS controlled-airspace constraints near Changi, Paya Lebar, Seletar, Tengah (digest open question) or Infrastructure Protection Act restrictions on MRT worksites prevent or delay fortnightly flights
risks.mitigation: Surface engine accepts total-station/GNSS-rover point CSVs and LandXML from any source; for restricted sites use KKL surveyor strut-level/grid surveys (same engine, lower density); pick pilot bulk sites outside restricted zones first; vendor handles permits in year 1

risks.risk: Main contractors refuse to accept a shared drone surface as the joint-measurement record and insist on their own surveyor's method
risks.mitigation: KKL's own surface still replaces the internal progress takeoff and gives an evidence pack; JM pack offers 10 random check cells for MC total-station verification; fall back to MC's method as the paid quantity with the engine in shadow, which still builds the ledger; ask MCs whether they already fly drones (digest open question)

risks.risk: DR rows lack chainage/depth band/loads or are not DR-Verified, so roll-ups are incomplete and the digest's 'zero extra data entry' promise fails
risks.mitigation: Reconcile tab flags coverage per contract; a class is not promoted past assist on a contract with <90% verified coverage; site coaching driven by the coverage report; delivery notes remain a second source

risks.risk: Contract preamble pays bulk excavation on design-nett quantities, not survey, so surface volumes are evidence rather than the claim quantity
risks.mitigation: bq_map paid_on field per item; for design-nett items the engine computes design surface vs baseline (deterministic) and uses survey for progress percentage and dispute evidence; PSSCOC Module A remeasurement still relies on measured executed work

risks.risk: Loads x capacity / bulking residual never stabilises (truck fill variance, fluff, part loads; payload sensors +/-3-5%) and QSs are tempted to treat loads as the quantity
risks.mitigation: Loads are a KPI and cross-check only, never the claim source for m3 items unless the preamble pays per load; residual >10% holds the line for review; calibrate bulking per soil_type from 3+ cycles before using the cross-check tolerance

risks.risk: Survey-volume error from vegetation, standing water, machines, stockpiles inside the zone (bare-ground vertical RMSE ~0.15 m without dense control, digest topic 6)
risks.mitigation: Exclusion masks per cycle; 10 cm noise threshold; GCPs/RTK required in vendor spec; vendor accuracy report attached to each surface; JM disputes >3% trigger joint total-station re-check of that zone

risks.risk: One part-time builder overloaded; scope creep into servers and drawing AI
risks.mitigation: Everything ships as single-file apps + one local Python package; no server, no database beyond CSV on SharePoint; tender plug-in gated behind month 9 and only after claims are in assist on 5 contracts; fixed weekly hours logged

risks.risk: Automation bias and deskilling: QSs accept generated packs without checking; escaped error reaches an SO or subcon dispute
risks.mitigation: Top-80%-of-value lines always human-checked; blind-then-reveal on a 20% sample; seeded known-error lines with catch-rate target >=90%; one fully manual pack per QS per quarter; rollback of a class to assist on any money-bearing error (> max(2% of line, S$2,000)); named QS signs every claim

risks.risk: Confidentiality breach: client drawings, BQ text or site surfaces sent to a cloud model on an NDA/OSA-restricted contract
risks.mitigation: Surfaces and drawings never leave the office PC; only tickets/DOs (KKL's own) and BQ text on contracts tagged 'may upload' go to the API; NDA-gated LTA contracts get bq_map typed by hand; project tier tag checked in the app before any upload

risks.risk: Accuracy gates cannot be met because inter-QS variance is itself larger than the class tolerance (unknown today)
risks.mitigation: Stage 0 two-QS baseline sets the tolerance per class to the observed ceiling; promotion criteria are relative to that ceiling, not to the digest's 1/2/3/5% defaults

risks.risk: Effort saving is real but invisible because claims share of QS hours is smaller than the digest's 25-30% inference
risks.mitigation: Two-week time log in month 0 fixes the denominator; alternating-month A/B on the same contract measures the saving; reduction reported in logged minutes per claim pack, not self-report

key_claims: Monthly progress claims plus subcontractor certification consume roughly 25-30% of KKL QS hours today (digest topic 2, inference, low confidence); a two-week time log will show it is not below 15%.

TIN/2.5D surface differencing of fortnightly RTK drone surfaces (1-3 cm H, 2-5 cm V with GCPs) yields bulk excavation volumes that agree with main-contractor joint measurement within 3% per zone on KKL sites once machines, stockpiles and water are masked.

DR Capture rows on claim-relevant contracts carry chainage, depth band, soil type and loads on at least 90% of rows after DR Verify, so linear and count items can be rolled up to BQ lines without new data entry (assumption; unverified).

Precast delivery notes, weighbridge tickets, staging-ground receipts and concrete DOs give an independent second source for DR-PIPE/DR-RCU/DR-SUMP, RW-ACWC, EW-DISP and RC-CONC that agrees with DR roll-ups within 2-5%, so two-source agreement is a usable confidence proxy for deterministic pipelines.
At least half of KKL's main contractors on subcontract packages will accept a shared, hashed survey surface plus random check cells as the joint-measurement record (digest open question).

Loads x nominal capacity / (1 + bulking) reconciles to surveyed bank volume within +/-10% after per-soil-type calibration over 3 cycles, making DR loads a valid cross-check (digest: truck counts are systematically unreliable, so this may fail and loads would stay a KPI only).

Vendor RTK flights at S$2,500-5,000 per visit fortnightly on 2-3 bulk sites cost less than the QS and surveyor hours they replace plus the value of faster, better-evidenced SOPA claims (assumption; no KKL hourly cost in the digest).
CAAS operator/UAPL/activity permits can be obtained for most KKL sites with lead times compatible with a fortnightly cadence; controlled-airspace sites are a minority (digest open question).

One part-time builder (about 2 days a week) can ship the surface engine, reconcile tab and claim-pack generator in 18 weeks using only PyMuPDF/ezdxf/lxml/scipy/numpy/shapely and single-file web apps, because no drawing understanding is required for claims.

The same bq_map and calc layer built for claims serve tender takeoff without rework, so tender-side automation starts from month 9 with an already-populated item library and KKL-calibrated bulking and productivity factors.

Surface, DR and ticket processing entirely on-premises, with only KKL's own commercial documents sent to the Claude API, satisfies OSA/NDA obligations on public-sector contracts (to be confirmed by the contracts person per NDA).
why_this_wins: It attacks the work that recurs every month on ~30 contracts rather than the bursty tender work, so effort savings compound across the whole portfolio as soon as DR coverage exists, not one tender at a time. It needs no scale detection, legend learning, OCR or drawing AI to deliver first value, so the part-time builder can ship it in 18 weeks with libraries the digest already validated. Every claim quantity gets independent ground truth within weeks (SO certification, MC joint measurement, subcon acceptance), which makes it the fastest way to build the per-class accuracy ledger the graduation framework requires and to prove effort reduction in logged minutes. Money safety is structural: two independent sources per line, surfaces as the volume source with loads as a KPI, top-value lines always human-checked, a named QS signing, and an audit appendix that reconstructs any quantity for an SO or adjudicator. It fits KKL's stack exactly (DR Capture CSV, SharePoint, GitHub Pages single-file apps, the existing Claude workbench for tickets) and Singapore realities (PSSCOC remeasurement, SOP Act monthly cadence, LTA M&W baseline survey, staging-ground tonnage by stream, OSA/NDA tiers by keeping drawings and surfaces on-premises). Finally, it leaves the tender side with a populated BQ item map, calibrated bulking and productivity factors and the spike extractors ready to plug in, so drawing-based automation starts from a stronger position than any drawing-first design.

name: Rulebook: preamble-driven quantity engine for KKL
angle: CALCULATION-FIRST (rules engine). Measure or type four primitives once; generate every derived BQ line, claim roll-up, subcon certificate and VO differential from a versioned, unit-tested rules engine keyed to KKL activity codes and a per-contract rulebook extracted from the BQ preambles and confirmed by the QS. Automate the primitives last, behind the same interface.
thesis:
The digest's inventory says the QS's hours do not go into drawing lines; they go into the arithmetic and the bookkeeping around them. Within tender takeoff, the heavy blocks are CIS RC drain/culvert build-ups (15%), trench and drain runs "and their derived excavation/backfill/disposal" (15-20%), and BQ entry and reconciliation in Excel (15-20%); outside tender work, monthly SOPA claims and subcon certification are 25-30% of all QS hours and recur on ~30 contracts every month (digest, QS inventory, marked medium/low inference). The same inventory concludes that ~60% of KKL's BQ lines (trench excavation by depth band, backfill, disposal, bedding, lean, formwork, concrete, asphalt tonnage, kerb haunch) are formulas over four primitives (polygon area, polyline length with attributes, count with attributes, volume from levels) plus LTA SDRE lookups and contract preambles, and says they "should be generated, versioned and unit-tested as code, never measured by a model". The calc_trench.py spike already shows the ratio: 25 primitives (4 lengths, 4 sizes, 8 level pairs, 1 count) produce ~20 BQ lines. This design makes that ratio the product: a rulebook per contract, an engine that turns primitives into BQ lines, and the same item mapping reused for claims, subcon certificates and VOs.

Why this is the safest and fastest route to falling QS effort: deterministic derived lines do not need a statistical accuracy gate the way AI measurement does. Their correctness rests on (a) the rulebook parameters being the contract's (each carries a page citation from the Price Document preambles and a QS confirmation), (b) golden regression tests on the engine, and (c) a shadow comparison against the QS's own hand calculation. Once those pass, a whole family of lines (EW-EXCT by band, EW-BF, EW-DISP, EW-HARD, RC-LEAN, RC-FW, RC-CONC, RC-REB from BBS, RW-SUB/BASE/ACBC/ACWC tonnage, RW-KERB haunch) becomes unsupervised except for input checks, and effort falls by the whole family, not one item class at a time. Money-bearing safety comes from keeping every input that requires judgement human (scale per viewport, level reading from long-sections, soil-class split, working space and temporary works allowances, VO rate choice, claim sign-off) and making every output reproducible: each quantity records engine version, rulebook version and primitive hash, so any line can be rebuilt for an SO or a subcontractor dispute. Under PSSCOC Module A the quantities are estimates remeasured as variations (digest, SG standards), so the named QS still signs; the engine changes what they sign from a spreadsheet they built to a report they audited.

The second half of the design is reconciliation, not measurement. KKL's DR Capture rows already carry activity_code, struct, method, spec_element, iw_mm/w_mm/depth_mm, ch_from_m/ch_to_m, depth_band, soil_type, spoil_to, loads and qty/unit (index.html CSVHEAD), i.e. the same keys the item library uses. A claim is therefore a roll-up: DR rows for the period, joined to BQ items through the item mapping, with chainage-interval union to prevent double claiming, survey surfaces for EW-EXC where they exist and load counts as a cross-check (digest, earthworks topic). This recurs monthly on ~30 contracts and is where the earliest recurring saving sits. VOs become differential runs: two primitive sets (old revision, new revision) through the same rulebook produce omissions and additions as separate lists, priced in the BQ rate -> pro-rata -> star -> daywork order (digest, inventory).

Automating the primitives comes last and plugs in behind the same primitives.json interface: Bluebeam/Acrobat measurement annotations harvested nightly (spike extract_markups.py, exact on synthetic), DXF via ezdxf (exact, no scale), vector-PDF auto-measure with per-viewport scale and legend confirmation (spike exact on synthetic; real LTA sheets showed no layers, multiple scales per page, outline text), and LandXML/drone surface differencing for EW-EXC. Each of these enters the staged shadow/assist/confidence-gated/audit programme from the digest per item class and per source, while the engine downstream of them is already trusted. The QS's job moves from measurer-and-calculator to input owner and auditor.

components.name: Item library (takeoff/library/items.json)
components.role: KKL's own civil measurement taxonomy, because Singapore has no civil SMM (digest, SG standards). One record per BQ item shape: id, trade, kkl_code (EW-EXC, EW-EXCT, EW-EXCP, EW-BF, EW-DISP, EW-HARD, DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, DR-SUMP, DR-BC, DR-CONN, RW-KERB, RW-SUB, RW-BASE, RW-ACBC, RW-ACWC, RW-FP, RC-LEAN, RC-FW, RC-REB, RC-BRC, RC-CONC, DM-*), unit, band_set ref (contract bands ne 2/2-4/4-6 m or 0.25 m stages; DR bands <1.5/1.5-3/3-6/>6 m), attributes (dia, size, type, grade, thickness), inclusions[] (e.g. trench item includes backfill+disposal: yes/no), formula_id (family) and DR join keys (struct, method, spec_element). Seeded from 3-5 live Price Documents in week 1; grows by QS confirmation of unmatched BQ lines. Families: TRENCH, CHAMBER, RC-SECTION, PAVEMENT, KERB, SURFACE, DEMO, DISPOSAL.
components.tech: JSON with JSON-Schema (ajv in browser), versioned in the GitHub repo; edited through a table in the takeoff app, exported as CSV to SharePoint for the QS team.

components.name: Rulebook per contract (takeoff/rules/<contract>.json) and Preamble->Rules Extract preset
components.role: Machine-checkable preambles: measurement {nett:true, bulking:false, working_space {default 0.30 m, by_od table}, depth_band_edges, band_by max_depth|invert_depth, trench_length_over_chambers, excavation_for_channels separate|included, rounding {concrete step 0.1 up}, fabric_laps:false}; materials {pipe OD table, U-drain outer sizes 600-1500, kerb K2A/K2B unit 980 mm, pavement stacks by road type with SDRE sheet refs, asphalt density (assumption 2.35 t/m3 until the M&W value is confirmed), mesh kg/m2 resolved to the named standard (A10 6.16 vs 7.90 example)}; inclusions per item. Every parameter carries {value, source_page, extracted_by, confirmed_by, ts}. Produced by the existing Extract agent (ai/index.html) with the rulebook JSON schema as structured output over the preamble pages only (text, no drawings), shown as a diff against the client template (LTA / HDB SOR / PUB / MC back-to-back); the QS confirms each money-bearing parameter by opening its cited page. Unconfirmed parameters block the engine ('rulebook incomplete'). For Tier-A (no cloud) contracts the QS types the rulebook from the template by hand.
components.tech: Claude API structured output (JSON schema) via the existing workbench; JSON files in git with semver tags; diff view in the app.

components.name: Rules engine (takeoff/engine.js)
components.role: Pure functions primitives x rulebook -> BQ lines, one module used by the browser app, the claim roll-up and the tests. Port and extension of calc_trench.py: TRENCH (run length, size, GL/IL pairs at chambers -> station integration at 0.5 m -> EW-EXCT by band, EW-HARD bedding/surround, EW-BF, EW-DISP, DR-PIPE/DR-RCU/DR-BC m); CHAMBER (count x type x depth-to-invert stage -> DR-SUMP nr, EW-EXCP m3, and RC-LEAN/RC-FW/RC-CONC/RC-REB for CIS sumps by section template); RC-SECTION (length x section template from SDRE or contract detail -> RC-LEAN, RC-FW m2 both faces, RC-CONC m3 rounded up 0.1, RC-REB t from BBS totals or kg/m3 flagged as assumption, RC-BRC m2 nett); PAVEMENT (area x road-type layer stack -> RW-SUB, RW-BASE m2 at thickness, RW-ACBC/RW-ACWC m2 and tonnes via thickness x density with add/deduct per 6 mm); KERB (length x type -> RW-KERB m, haunch concrete m3, kerb trench m3); SURFACE (two TIN surfaces + boundary -> EW-EXC/EW-BF by band, grid difference); DEMO (DM-DRN m, DM-PAVE m2, DM-KERB m); DISPOSAL (EW-DISP = excavation - reuse, split by soil stream from SI percentages, tonnes at staging-ground fees). Emits per line: qty, unit, inputs used, rule parameters used, engine and rulebook versions, primitive hashes.
components.tech: Plain ES module JavaScript (no build step) so it runs inside a single-file GitHub Pages app; tests with node --test and golden files (takeoff/tests/*.golden.json) including the existing sample_drawing.truth.json; CI on GitHub Actions blocks a release when any golden line changes.

components.name: Primitive capture app (takeoff/index.html)
components.role: Where primitives enter and outputs leave. Four input modes: (1) typed tables for QSs who measure in Bluebeam/Excel today: runs (id, code, spec, length, chainage from/to, zone), chamber levels (GL, IL per chamber), areas, counts; (2) on-sheet trace with pdf.js: polyline/polygon/count with snapping to vector paths, per-viewport scale object seeded from title-block text and page size, confirmed by the QS with an OpenTakeoff-style dimension/scale-bar check (green <=1%, amber <=5%, export blocked >5%); (3) import Bluebeam/Acrobat measurement annotations harvested by the nightly job (subject = KKL code via a tool-set file); (4) import DXF primitives from the on-prem ezdxf script. Cross-checks on entry: sum of run lengths vs drain schedule total (Extract agent reads the schedule with citations), IL monotonic along a run, GL-IL depth within band range, area vs sheet extents. Outputs: BQ quantity sheet, claim pack, subcon certificate, VO report, accuracy ledger rows. Every primitive: {sheet_hash, page, viewport, scale, geometry, code, attrs{dia,size,type,gl,il,ch_from,ch_to,zone}, source typed|trace|bluebeam|dxf|auto, confirmed_by}.
components.tech: Single-file HTML on GitHub Pages like DR Capture; pdfjs-dist 4.10.38 pinned (spike note on 5.x/6.x); SheetJS 0.20.x from cdnjs for .xlsx; localStorage drafts; primitives.json + CSV uploaded to the project's SharePoint folder the same way DR Capture uploads Site Logs.

The same binding is reused for the claim pack and the VO report so tender, claim and VO quantities join on one key.

components.name: Claim roll-up and subcon certificate (takeoff/claims.html)
components.role: Monthly SOPA claim per contract: reads DR Capture/DR Verify CSVs from SharePoint (CSVHEAD fields), joins (activity_code, struct, method, spec_element, depth_band) to BQ items via the item library, unions chainage intervals per run to prevent double claiming, computes this-period and cumulative per BQ item against provisional quantities, ingests survey volumes (LandXML/CSV from Kubla/TBC/drone vendor) for EW-EXC zones with load counts x capacity / bulking as the cross-check residual, and lists the DR row ids behind every line as the SOPA 'work done' record. Subcon certificate = same rows filtered by subcon flag and codes (RW-ACBC, RW-ACWC, RW-MARK, RC-*) with back-to-back or subcon rates.

components.name: Auto-measure (phase 2 of primitives)

components.name: Accuracy ledger and gate dashboard
components.role: One row per BQ line per run: item class, source, engine qty, QS final qty, delta, time-on-sheet per class (explicit start/pause timer), reviewer, audit outcome. A single-file page reads the ledger CSV and shows per class x source: median and p95 error, count exact-match, automation rate, audited accuracy, escaped errors, minutes per sheet, and the current stage with its rollback triggers.

architecture.data_flow: Tender: Price Document PDF (GeBIZ ZIP) -> BQ binder (Extract agent, text only) -> bq.json + preamble pages -> Preamble->Rules preset -> rulebook draft -> QS confirms parameters against cited pages -> rulebook v1 tagged. Drawings stay local: QS types/traces primitives in takeoff/index.html (or the nightly harvester imports Bluebeam markups / ezdxf reads DXF) -> primitives.json with per-viewport scale confirmed -> engine.js (primitives x rulebook x item library) -> BQ quantity sheet .xlsx with engine vs QS columns -> QS reconciles, signs, files; ledger rows written. Claims: DR Capture CSVs + survey surfaces from SharePoint -> claims.html joins to bq.json via item library -> claim pack and subcon certificate .xlsx -> QS signs -> SharePoint. VOs: revision-B primitives -> engine diff -> omissions/additions report. Later: auto-measure produces primitives with source=auto into the same file; the ledger compares them with the QS's and moves classes through shadow -> assist -> auto-with-audit.
inputs: GeBIZ Price Schedule / BQ PDFs with preambles (text pages may go to the Claude API on Tier-B/C contracts)
Tender and construction drawings: vector PDF (primary), scans (traced by QS), DXF/DWG when supplied (exact route), LandXML surfaces when requested from Civil 3D users
Drain/pipe/sump schedules and long-sections (levels read by QS or extracted with citations)
BBS totals for RC-REB when issued; kg/m3 assumption flagged otherwise
LTA SDRE (KER/DRA/PAV sheets), LTA M&W chapters, PUB COP, HDB SOR preambles as the reference library
DR Capture / DR Verify CSVs (CSVHEAD fields) and the machine register from SharePoint
Survey volumes (LandXML/CSV) from KKL or vendor drone/total-station surveys; disposal tickets, DOs, weighbridge tickets
Bluebeam/Acrobat marked-up PDFs in the tender and claims folders
SI borehole strata per zone (existing blueprint Extract preset) for the disposal split
outputs: BQ quantity sheet (.xlsx/CSV): item no, description, unit, engine qty, QS qty, delta, inputs, rule refs, versions
Monthly SOPA claim pack per contract and subcontractor certificates (.xlsx) with DR row ids behind every line
VO differential report: omissions and additions per BQ item with pricing-basis column
Material order quantities (concrete m3 by pour, rebar t, pipe m by dia, kerb units) from the same lines
primitives.json and rulebook.json per tender (reproducibility record)
Accuracy ledger CSV and gate dashboard

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Nothing in production. Stage 0 instrumentation (per-sheet per-class timer, two-QS baseline on ~20 sheets), item library v0 from 3-5 live BQs, rulebook for 2 contracts, engine TRENCH/CHAMBER families in shadow on 2-3 live tenders (QS commits their own figure first, then sees the engine's).
effort_curve.qs_role: Measurer and calculator as today; additionally confirms rulebook parameters and types primitives for the shadow run (about +5% effort on pilot tenders).
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Baseline established: minutes per sheet per class, inter-QS disagreement per class (this is the ceiling the engine is judged against; digest HITL). Gate to Stage 2 for a derived family: >=200 lines across >=3 tenders, every engine-vs-QS difference root-caused as QS slip, rule gap or engine bug (bug -> golden test added), zero unexplained differences, all golden tests green.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Derived families TRENCH, CHAMBER, PAVEMENT, KERB and RC-SECTION in Stage 2 (engine drafts, QS verifies each line) on all new tenders; BQ binder pre-fills the quantity sheet; claim roll-up in shadow on 2 contracts, assist on 1; VO differential available. Counts from schedules via Extract agent in Stage 2.
effort_curve.qs_role: Enters primitives (typed or traced), confirms rulebook, reviews every generated line; still builds claims by hand except on the pilot contract.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Evidence: timer shows tender-takeoff minutes per sheet for the derived families down by >=40% versus baseline on alternating-sheet A/B; ledger shows zero money-bearing errors (>2% of item value or >S$10k tender line / >S$2k claim line, digest definition) in engine lines. Gate to Stage 3 for a family: 300 clean lines, audited accuracy of engine lines >=99.5%, rulebook coverage of that family's parameters 100% confirmed.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Derived families in Stage 3 (auto-accepted, 10% random audit decaying to 5%, value-based always-check on the top 80% of value); claim roll-ups in assist on ~15 contracts and auto-draft with QS sign on the 5 longest-running; subcon certificates on asphalt and RC subcons; Bluebeam markup harvest feeding primitives; DXF route in Stage 2 for counts and lengths; vector-PDF auto counts and lengths in shadow/assist per source.
effort_curve.qs_role: Input owner and auditor: confirms scale per viewport, reads levels, sets soil split, audits sampled lines, signs claims; measures one full sheet per week unassisted (deskilling control).
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Evidence: total logged QS minutes per S$1m measured down ~25-30%; claim pack preparation time on pilot contracts down >=50%; escaped-error rate on auto-accepted lines <=0.5%. Gates for measured primitives (per class x source, digest): >=200 items or >=30 sheets across >=5 projects, median abs error <=1% vector/DXF or <=3% scan, p95 <=5%, count exact-match >=98%, zero confident-wrong items, calibration checked.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Everything derived is Stage 3/4 with audit; counts and lengths from DXF and vector PDF Stage 3; areas from vector PDF Stage 2 moving to 3 where the gate passes; EW-EXC from survey surfaces computed by code with QS ownership (Stage 2, indefinitely); claims auto-drafted on all ~30 contracts; VOs are differential runs plus QS valuation; material orders generated from the same lines. Scans remain QS-traced with snapping.
effort_curve.qs_role: Estimator, reviewer, exception handler, signatory. Human forever: rulebook confirmation, scale/viewport confirmation, level reading on scans, soil-class and working-space judgement, under-strut staging (EW-EXCTD), VO rate choice, dispute handling, claim signature.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Evidence: ledger shows 15-20% of items still human-touched even in graduated classes (expected steady state, digest); audited accuracy per class published monthly; rollback triggers exercised at least once and recovered (any money-bearing error -> class back to Stage 2 until 300 clean items; audit error rate >2x baseline -> audit rate to 10%; new drawing source -> review until 50 clean items; any engine/rulebook/library change -> full golden re-run).

costs.licences_and_services: No new licences required: GitHub Pages (free), SharePoint/Microsoft 365 (existing), one office PC for the nightly harvester and DXF/LandXML scripts (existing). Open-source only: pdf.js 4.10.38, SheetJS, PyMuPDF 1.28, ezdxf 1.4.4, LibreDWG (GPL, separate process), lxml, scipy/numpy. Claude API for preamble extraction, BQ-line classification and schedule/legend reads: roughly 5 tenders/month x (US$1 preamble extract + US$2 BQ classification + US$1 schedules) plus claims text reads, about US$50-100/month at the blueprint's rates (Opus 5 US$5/25 per M tokens; Sonnet 5 lane for routine extraction), budgeted at US$150 with headroom. Builder effort assumption: about 0.4 FTE for months 1-6 (~10 person-weeks), ~10 person-weeks months 7-12, ~16 person-weeks months 13-24; chief QS ~8 person-weeks over 24 months for library, rulebooks and audits (assumption). Optional: Bluebeam Core US$330/user/year if QSs do not already have measurement-capable PDF tools; Kreo Pro US$175/month only as a benchmark; RTK drone survey S$2.5-10k per visit charged to the project that uses it.

risks.risk: The ~60% 'formula lines' share does not hold on KKL's actual BQs (digest figure is an inference), so the engine covers fewer lines than planned
risks.mitigation: Week-1 count of BQ lines by family on 3-5 live Price Documents before committing the build order; the plan still stands on claims roll-up and BQ binding even if the derived share is 40%

risks.risk: Preamble ambiguity: two QSs read 'trench length measured over sumps' or working-space rules differently, and the engine encodes one reading
risks.mitigation: Rulebook parameters carry page citations and a named confirmer; diff against the client template highlights departures; shadow differences are root-caused to rule interpretation and resolved by the chief QS before Stage 2; per-contract rulebooks, never a global one

risks.risk: Garbage in: a mistyped level, wrong pipe size or wrong viewport scale propagates into twenty generated lines
risks.mitigation: Entry cross-checks (IL monotonic, depth within band range, run totals vs schedule, scale-bar grader blocking export >5%), two-source agreement where available (Bluebeam markup vs typed), value-based always-check on the top 80% of value, and every line traceable to its primitives

risks.risk: An engine bug ships and silently changes many lines across tenders
risks.mitigation: Golden regression corpus (synthetic truth plus every QS-corrected real line), CI blocking release on any golden change, engine and rulebook versions stamped on every quantity, differential re-run of past tenders after any release, class back to shadow for 100 items on any regression (digest trigger 4)

risks.risk: Automation bias and deskilling once lines are auto-accepted
risks.mitigation: Blind-then-reveal on a 20% sample, seeded known-error lines with catch rate tracked (>=90%), one fully manual sheet per QS per week, juniors in Stage 2 with reveal disabled for 6 months, reviewers scored on catch rate not throughput (digest HITL)

risks.risk: DR Capture data on some contracts is too coarse (missing chainage, mixed codes) for a defensible claim roll-up
risks.mitigation: Per-contract gate (>=95% rows with chainage or zone, 3 months within 2% of the QS claim) before assist; validation rules pushed back into DR Capture; claims never auto-submitted

risks.risk: QSs keep working in Excel/Bluebeam and do not enter primitives in the new app
risks.mitigation: Typed tables mirror their spreadsheets, outputs are .xlsx, and the nightly harvester turns their existing Bluebeam markups into primitives with no behaviour change; tool-set file maps subjects to KKL codes

risks.risk: Confidentiality: a drawing from an OSA/NDA contract reaches a cloud model
risks.mitigation: Geometry and measurement never leave the browser/LAN; only preamble and BQ text go to the API and only on Tier-B/C projects; project tier is checked before any Extract run; Tier-A rulebooks typed from templates

risks.risk: Single part-time builder is the bottleneck and a single point of failure
risks.mitigation: Same single-file discipline as DR Capture; engine is a pure module with tests and a README; rulebooks and item library are data edited by the QS team, not code; scope sequenced so each milestone is usable on its own

risks.risk: Automated primitives from real vector PDFs underperform (no layers, several scales per sheet, outline text, as seen on LTA SDRE sheets)
risks.mitigation: Primitives automation is scheduled after the engine and claims already deliver value; per-source graduation with the digest gates; DXF requested wherever possible; QS tracing with snapping remains the permanent fallback

risks.risk: Rebar quantities (RC-REB) wrong when no BBS is issued and a kg/m3 assumption is used
risks.mitigation: Lines derived from assumptions are flagged in the output and excluded from Stage 3; RC-REB graduates only from BBS totals

key_claims: At least 50% of BQ lines by count (and at least 40% by value) on KKL's LTA/HDB/PUB Price Documents are deterministic functions of the four primitives plus the rulebook and SDRE lookups (digest inference ~60%; refutable by the week-1 count on 3-5 live BQs).

The measurement preambles of KKL's live contracts can be captured as a rulebook of no more than ~40 parameters per contract (depth-band edges and basis, working-space table, bedding/surround, rounding, inclusions, length-over-chambers, fabric laps, densities) without free-text exceptions that the engine cannot apply (refutable by encoding 3 contracts in weeks 3-5).

A QS can enter or trace the primitives for the TRENCH, CHAMBER, RC-SECTION and PAVEMENT families in no more than 30-40% of the time they currently spend producing those families' full BQ quantities by hand (assumption; refutable by the Stage 0 timer and alternating-sheet A/B in months 3-6).

Engine-vs-QS disagreement on derived lines, after rule interpretation is reconciled, is smaller than inter-QS disagreement on the same lines (refutable by the two-QS baseline versus the shadow ledger).

DR Capture rows already carry enough keys (activity_code, struct, method, spec_element, ch_from_m/ch_to_m or zone, depth_band, qty/unit) to roll up to at least 80% of claimable BQ items on a pilot contract without additional site data entry (refutable on the two shadow claim contracts in months 3-5).

Bluebeam/Acrobat measurement annotations in KKL's real marked-up PDFs can be read by PyMuPDF into primitives with subject-to-code mapping and per-viewport scale (spike proved this on synthetic annotations only; refutable on one real KKL PDF in weeks 15-18).

Deterministic derived lines can be promoted to auto-accept on the basis of rulebook confirmation plus golden tests plus a 300-clean-line shadow/assist record, with an escaped money-bearing error rate at or below 0.5% (refutable by the audit stream in months 8-12).

Vector-PDF auto-measurement of counts and lengths on KKL's real sheets reaches median error <=1% and count exact-match >=98% per drawing source after per-viewport scale and legend confirmation (spike exact on synthetic; real LTA sheets showed no layers and mixed scales; refutable in the month 6-10 shadow).

A browser-only single-file app on GitHub Pages plus CSV/JSON on SharePoint and one on-prem PC for nightly harvesting is sufficient infrastructure for the full 24-month scope; no server, database or cloud drawing processing is needed (refutable if project sizes exceed browser memory or if multi-user concurrency on one tender becomes necessary).

Reusing one item mapping for tender, claim, subcon certificate and VO produces claim packs that main contractors and SOs accept with no more queries than today's spreadsheets (refutable by query counts on the pilot contracts).
why_this_wins: It attacks the hours that are actually large and recurring (derived BQ lines, BQ entry and reconciliation, monthly claims on ~30 contracts, VO differentials) with code whose correctness rests on confirmed contract rules and unit tests rather than on an AI accuracy programme, so first value arrives in weeks and whole families of money-bearing lines graduate together. Every judgement input stays human and every output is reproducible to engine version, rulebook version and primitive hash, which is what a named QS needs to sign under PSSCOC Module A and the SOP Act. It fits the builder and the stack exactly (single-file apps, CSV to SharePoint, existing Extract agent for preambles), needs no new licences, satisfies OSA/NDA confidentiality by never sending geometry to the cloud, and reuses KKL's own DR Capture keys as the item taxonomy. Measurement automation (Bluebeam harvest, DXF, vector PDF, surfaces) plugs in later behind the same primitives.json interface and passes through the digest's shadow/assist/confidence-gated/audit gates per class and source, so the effort curve keeps falling after the calculation win without ever re-opening the safety argument downstream.

name: KKL Takeoff Overlay — the in-house civils.ai (VLM reads, code measures, QS confirms on canvas)
angle: VLM-hybrid product: grow ai/index.html into a takeoff product where a vision-language model classifies and reads (legend, schedules, title block, sheet index, revision diffs, BQ line mapping), deterministic geometry measures (PyMuPDF/pdf.js paths, ezdxf entities, calc layer), small fine-tuned detectors count recurring symbols on scans, and the QS confirms every item on an overlay canvas with per-item confidence, cost readout and a 'checked by' stamp. Every confirmation is a label; per-client templates capture the standard; a confidentiality gateway decides what may leave the laptop.
thesis:
KKL's quantities are, in the digest's words, mostly calculations over four primitives (polygon area, polyline length with attributes, count with attributes, surface volume from levels) plus SDRE/M&W lookups and BQ preambles; ~60% of BQ lines are formulas over those primitives. The spikes in /home/user/kkl-dr/takeoff/ already prove that on vector PDF and DXF the primitives come out exactly with no AI at all (all eight items exact on sample_drawing.pdf via PyMuPDF and pdf.js; DXF exact via ezdxf), while the state of the art says frontier VLMs read text on drawings at 0.90-0.95 but count symbols at 0.40-0.55 and hallucinate on structured extraction. So the product splits the work by what each component is provably good at: the VLM never emits a number that becomes a quantity; it emits labels, mappings, regions and cross-checks (which legend symbol is a sump, which schedule row is DR-PIPE 450, what the title block says the scale is, which BQ line this maps to, what changed between Rev B and Rev C). Deterministic code measures lengths, areas and counts from paths, blocks and hatches; a generalised calc_trench.py turns confirmed primitives plus a per-contract rule set (working space, bedding, depth bands, nett measurement, rounding) into EW-EXCT/EW-BF/EW-DISP/EW-HARD/DR-*/RW-*/RC-* lines. A small YOLO-family detector, trained on crops that QSs confirm, counts sumps, DICs and manholes on scans where there is no vector geometry.

The QS's daily surface is an overlay canvas, not a chat box. The sheet renders through pdf.js 4.10.38 (pinned, as in ai/index.html); on top of it an SVG overlay shows every proposed item as coloured geometry keyed to a KKL activity code, with a right-hand item list carrying quantity, unit, five confidence chips (scale confirmed, two routes agree, legend unambiguous, label attached, VLM verdict), a cost readout (qty x KKL rate) and a status. The QS accepts, edits, splits or rejects items with single keys, calibrates scale per viewport, and ends the sheet with a 'checked by' stamp that locks it and writes rows to SharePoint as CSV, in the same style as DR Verify. Every accept, edit and reject is a labelled example (sheet hash, viewport, path ids, signature, code, QS decision, minutes) and every edit is a regression case, so the classifier, the legend library, the detector and the confidence calibration improve from the takeoffs QSs already do, without a separate labelling programme. The nightly Bluebeam markup harvester (extract_markups.py, run on the tender and claims folders via Graph delta query) adds labels from QSs who keep measuring in Revu.

Money stays safe through the digest's five-stage programme applied per item class and per drawing source, enforced in the UI rather than in a policy document: shadow (engine measures blind, QS does not see it until they commit), assist (engine pre-fills, QS verifies every item), confidence-gated (auto-accept above a per-class threshold calibrated on Stage 1 data, 10% random audit decaying to 2%, top-80%-of-value always human, hard rollback triggers), and autonomous-with-audit. Graduation gates are numbers the ledger computes from the label store (count exact-match >=98%, median absolute error <=1% vector / <=3% scan, p95 <=5%, zero confident-wrong, >=200 then >=500 items across >=5 projects and >=2 sources). A named QS signs every sheet at every stage because PSSCOC Module A makes quantities the contractor's risk. The effect on effort is therefore stepwise and evidenced: a class only stops costing QS minutes when its own numbers say so.

Confidentiality is a first-class architectural decision, not an afterthought: geometry extraction and measurement run on the QS's laptop (pdf.js) or on an office box (PyMuPDF/ezdxf/YOLO) and never leave KKL; the only egress is the VLM call, and a per-project tier set by the contracts person at intake decides whether that call may happen at all (T0 own/public documents: any cloud; T1 client tender documents without NDA/OSA marking: cloud with zero-retention terms and region pinning, sending crops and text rather than full sets; T2 NDA/OSA/IPA rail and depot work: no cloud, the QS binds the legend by hand in the canvas and local OCR does the text). This is the one thing civils.ai (US servers) and Kreo (cloud) structurally cannot offer KKL, and it is what makes the in-house route the only route for a share of KKL's contracts regardless of cost.

components.name: Ingest and router
components.role: Turns every incoming drawing into one internal sheet model (per page: viewports with scale+unit, layers, paths with width/colour/dash/closure, text with position and direction, images) and classifies the sheet: vector-with-text, vector-with-outline-text (words==0 with thousands of small fills), scan, DXF. Records source type per sheet for the per-source accuracy ledger.
components.tech: PyMuPDF 1.28 get_cdrawings()/get_drawings(extended=True) (0.85-2.4 s for 120k segments; clip hierarchy for viewports; OCG layer per path), get_text('dict') with line direction, get_ocgs(); ezdxf 1.4.4 for DXF (INSERT counts, LWPOLYLINE/HATCH via ezdxf.path, DIMENSION.get_measurement(), viewport scale, $INSUNITS); LibreDWG dwg2dxf (GPLv3) or its WASM build for DWG (ODA File Converter only if commercial terms confirmed); 300 dpi render (0.63 s per A1) for scans and outline-text pages; PaddleOCR with use_textline_orientation for rotated labels on T2 sheets. components.role: Deterministic measurement: clusters paths by signature (stroke colour, width bucket 0.36/0.72/1.08/1.44 pt, dash, closed, fill), binds signatures to legend entries, excludes legend box and title block, resolves scale per viewport (title-block seed + dimension-string vote + scale bar), attaches nearest run label, measures length/area/count, and runs the same sheet through pdf.js as a second route so two-route agreement within 1% becomes a confidence check.
components.tech: Python on the local runner (PyMuPDF path) and JavaScript in the browser (pdf.js 4.10.38 getOperatorList with a graphics-state stack, as in extract_pdfjs.mjs); shapely for polygon ops; OpenTakeoff-style 'check a dimension' grader (green within 1%, amber within 5%, block export beyond) as the acceptance test per viewport.

components.name: VLM reader
components.role: Reads, classifies and cross-checks; never measures. Tasks: sheet index and sheet-type classification; title block (scale, sheet no., revision, title, client); legend entries returned as text + bbox so the measurer can crop the symbol and learn its signature; schedules (drain, sump/DIC, pipe, BBS totals) as JSON with page citations; BQ Price Schedule PDF to structured BQ (item no., description hierarchy, unit, provisional qty, rate); preamble rules to a per-contract rule-set draft; revision diff narrative between two sheets; a count 'opinion' used only to flag disagreement with the geometry count.

components.name: Symbol detector
components.role: Counts recurring symbols on scans and outline-text sheets (DR-SUMP, DR-BC, DICs, scuppers, lamp posts, kerb-type ticks) and cross-checks vector counts. Emits boxes with confidence; the QS accepts on the canvas.

components.name: Calc layer and rule sets
components.role: Turns confirmed primitives into BQ lines in KKL codes: trench excavation by depth band (EW-EXCT), backfill (EW-BF), bedding/surround (EW-HARD), disposal (EW-DISP), pipe/U-drain lengths by size and depth stage (DR-PIPE, DR-RCU), sumps by depth (DR-SUMP), kerb by type (RW-KERB), pavement layers by SDRE road-type thickness (RW-SUB, RW-BASE, RW-ACWC, RW-FP), CIS culvert/drain concrete, formwork and rebar from SDRE section lookups (RC-CONC, RC-FW, RC-REB). architecture.data_flow: 1) Intake: contracts person tags the project tier (T0/T1/T2) and the client template; the QS drops the GeBIZ ZIP (PDF drawings, Price Schedule PDF), any DXF/DWG/LandXML, and scans into the project folder on SharePoint. 2) Ingest on the local runner (or in-browser for T2/offline) produces sheet.json per page with source type; the VLM reader (tier permitting) returns sheet index, title-block fields, legend entries with bboxes, schedules and the structured BQ with page citations, using global thumbnail + crops. 3) The measurer binds legend bboxes to path signatures, resolves a scale object per viewport (seeded from the title block, refined by dimension strings, checked against the scale bar), clusters and measures, attaches labels, and runs the second route; the detector adds boxes on scans; each item gets a composite confidence from verifiable checks. 4) The canvas shows items per sheet; in Stage 1 quantities are hidden until the QS commits their own; in Stage 2+ the QS accepts/edits/rejects; the QS confirms scale and legend binding once per viewport; the calc layer immediately derives the dependent BQ lines from the contract rule set; the BQ strip shows our qty vs provisional qty per BQ item. 5) 'Checked by' stamps the sheet; takeoff_items.csv, takeoff_labels.csv and takeoff_audit.csv go to SharePoint; the annotated PDF with /Measure markups and the BQ Excel go to the project folder. 6) Nightly: the harvester pulls Bluebeam markups from tender/claims folders as extra labels; the ledger recomputes per-class x source metrics, stage, thresholds and audit samples; crops for symbol families accumulate for detector training; regressions run on every code, prompt or model change. 7) Monthly: DR Capture rows and tickets roll up into claim lines on the same keys; survey volumes replace theoretical volumes where a surface exists; the same ledger scores claim-pack agreement.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Stage 0 instrumentation done (timer, edit log, two-QS baseline on 20 sheets); canvas live in assist mode for counts (DR-SUMP, DR-BC on DXF and vector PDF) and VLM schedule/BQ/title-block reads with citations; scale objects seeded; linear runs in shadow only. Bluebeam harvester running.
effort_curve.qs_role: Measurer as today, plus confirming counts and schedule rows on the canvas and calibrating scale per viewport; chief QS builds LTA/HDB/PUB templates.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Evidence: minutes per sheet per class logged from week 2; counts and schedule reads are under 10% of tender hours (digest inventory), so saving is small; BQ-to-structured extraction removes part of the 15-20% BQ entry/reconciliation block only once mapping accept-without-edit >=90% on the three-tender eval set.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Counts and schedule reads at Stage 3 on DXF/vector PDF (auto-accept above threshold, 10% audit); BQ line extraction and KKL-code mapping at Stage 2-3; linear runs DR-PIPE/DR-RCU at Stage 2 (pre-filled, QS verifies) with the calc layer generating EW-EXCT/EW-BF/EW-HARD/EW-DISP lines from confirmed runs and levels; areas in shadow; claim roll-up from DR rows in assist on 5 contracts.
effort_curve.qs_role: Reviewer for counts/schedules/BQ mapping; verifier for linear runs; still measures areas and volumes by hand; signs every sheet.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Gate to Stage 3 for counts: >=200 items across >=5 projects and >=2 sources, count exact-match >=98%, zero confident-wrong, calibration checked. Gate to Stage 2 for linear: >=200 items, median abs error <=1% (vector/DXF), p95 <=5%, scale check green (<=1%) on every viewport. Effort figure assumes the trench/drain block (15-20% of tender hours) halves in QS minutes at Stage 2 and BQ entry falls by a third; both to be read off the timer, not self-report.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: DR-PIPE, DR-RCU, RW-KERB at Stage 3 on vector PDF/DXF with dependent calc lines auto-generated; RW-ACWC/RW-FP/RW-SUB/RW-BASE at Stage 2-3; VO revision diff in assist; RC-CONC/RC-FW/RC-REB for CIS drains/culverts via SDRE lookups at Stage 2; scan counts via detector at Stage 2 for families with >=2,000 instances; monthly claim packs at Stage 3 for DR-derived lines with ticket reconciliation on most contracts; bulk EW-EXC from LandXML/DXF surfaces at Stage 2 where surfaces exist.
effort_curve.qs_role: Exception handler and estimator: works the review queue (below-threshold items and the top-80%-of-value items), prices, checks calc rule sets per tender, owns VO valuation; one fully manual sheet per week per QS for skill maintenance.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Gate to Stage 3 per class: >=500 verified items, accept-without-edit >=95%, escaped-error rate <=0.5%, no money-bearing error (>2% of item value or >S$2,000 claims / >S$10,000 tender line) in the last 300 items, threshold derived from observed confidence distribution. Areas additionally require mean signed error within ±1% (Togal study found systematic under-measurement). Effort figure: trench/drain block and kerb/pavement at review-only cost, calc lines free, claims roll-up replacing most of the 25-30% monthly-claims block's measurement time; A/B alternating-sheet assignment inside the same tender proves the delta.

effort_curve.what_is_automated: Counts, linear runs and areas at Stage 4 (2-5% audit) on vector PDF/DXF; scan counts at Stage 3; CIS RC build-ups at Stage 3; calc lines auto for all graduated primitives; BQ mapping Stage 4; claims roll-ups Stage 3-4 with survey-volume ingestion where drone/total-station surfaces exist; VO differential still Stage 2 (assist); EW-EXC from PDF contours/scanned sections stays Stage 2; disposal soil-class split stays assisted.
effort_curve.qs_role: Reviewer of last resort, estimator, claims negotiator; audits the auto-accepted stream; a named QS still signs every bid, claim and subcon certificate.
effort_curve.gate_or_evidence: Stage 4 per class: month 12+ with quarterly blind re-baseline, monthly drift review (PSI on confidence distribution and edit rate acted on only with an audit accuracy drop), audit at 2-5%. Steady state keeps 15-20% of items human-touched even in graduated classes (claims-processing benchmark in digest), and bulk-excavation volumes from sections (15-20% of tender hours) remain human-led, which caps the reduction near 40-45% of today's takeoff effort; the residual is judgement (soil class, working space, VO valuation) and signing.

risks.risk: Real consultant PDFs defeat signature clustering and legend binding (no layers, all-black linework, pen weights 0.36-2.16 pt, several scales per sheet, outline text) far more than the synthetic spike suggests, so linear runs never reach the Stage 2 gate
risks.mitigation: Regression corpus of real LTA/MC sheets from week 2; classification keyed on pen weight, dash, geometry and label proximity with QS corrections as training; per-viewport scale as a first-class object the QS confirms; push for DXF on every contract; the canvas still pays off as a fast confirm-and-label tool even if automation stalls

risks.risk: Scale mis-resolution on multi-scale detail sheets produces a confident wrong length (the dimension-vote heuristic recovered only 2 of 4 LTA sheets)
risks.mitigation: No quantity is exportable until the viewport's scale is QS-confirmed and the dimension check is green (<=1%); dimension-line detection (arrowheads/extension lines) added to raise automatic inference; scale confirmations stored as training data; any amber viewport routes the whole viewport to review

risks.risk: Confidentiality breach: a T2 sheet crop reaches a cloud model, or a client objects to any third-party processing
risks.mitigation: Tier set at intake by contracts; gateway refuses egress for T2 (no API key in T2 sessions); egress log per project; browser-only measurement path for T2 with manual legend binding; region-pinned/zero-retention endpoints recorded in the project file for T1; Singapore-region options (Vertex/Bedrock/inference_geo) evaluated before any Gemini lane is used

risks.risk: Automation bias and deskilling: QSs accept pre-filled items without checking (evidence: ~45% of errors under AI assistance from over-reliance; measured skill loss after months of AI use)
risks.mitigation: Blind-then-reveal on a 20% sample in Stages 2-4; seeded known-error items with catch rate >=90% per QS; one fully manual sheet per QS per week scored against the engine; juniors in reveal-disabled mode for 6 months; reviewers measured on catch rate not throughput

risks.risk: Areas systematically under-measured (independent Togal study: 12 of 15 items low) and volumes over-estimated (average-end-area +5-10%), causing bid losses that per-item tolerances miss
risks.mitigation: Mean signed error within ±1% as an explicit area gate; hatch-island tests in the corpus; volumes computed as surface differences, never end-area, with a per-project validation against Civil 3D/Propeller before use in a claim

risks.risk: VLM hallucination in schedules and BQ extraction (zero-shot recall 25-37% and hallucination up to 56% on structured drawing extraction) leaks into sizes, depths or units
risks.mitigation: Every extracted row must carry a citation; column sums must reconcile to stated totals; size/unit/band never auto-accepted when the VLM and the item library disagree; benchmark on KKL sheets before choosing the model; fine-tune a small open VLM (Florence-2 class) on KKL labels if recall stays low

why_this_wins: It is the only design that fits all three of KKL's hard constraints at once and still compounds. First, confidentiality: geometry and measurement never leave KKL's laptops or office box; the VLM call is the single egress and it is tier-gated per project, so OSA/NDA rail work is served by the same canvas with the VLM switched off. Buying civils.ai (US$270/user/month Professional, 30 takeoffs/month, US$9 per takeoff, US servers, human QA in 24 h, 1 takeoff = 1 trade per sheet up to 1:250, cut/fill 'coming soon') gives first value in days on T0 sheets and is cheaper than the builder's time for the first six months, but it cannot process T2 drawings, exposes no geometry or per-class accuracy, learns nothing from KKL's daily reports, and its 97% is self-reported; Kreo (US$35-175/month, Auto Measure categories are rooms/walls/openings, measurement API only on Pro/Enterprise) has no civil classes and is cloud-only. The honest recommendation is to trial civils.ai Starter (US$90/month) on T0 sheets for three months as an external benchmark for the in-house engine, not as the product. Second, safety: the staged shadow/assist/confidence-gated/audit framework lives inside the UI and the ledger, per class and per source, with numeric gates the chief QS can read, blind-then-reveal and seeded errors against automation bias, and a named QS stamp on every sheet, so money-bearing quantities are never a model's number. Third, feasibility: it grows from code KKL already has (ai/index.html, extract_pymupdf.py, extract_pdfjs.mjs, extract_dxf.py, calc_trench.py, extract_markups.py), in the single-file GitHub Pages plus CSV-to-SharePoint style the builder ships today, with the chief QS owning templates and rules as data. The label flywheel is free: every confirmation on the canvas and every Bluebeam markup in the tender folder is a label, and because the same keys (activity code, structure, element, chainage, depth band) are shared with DR Capture, the tender takeoff, the monthly claim and the subcon certificate join on one schema, which is the loop civils.ai cannot close and where 25-30% of QS hours sit. The result is a curve that is slow at month 6 (~88% of today), real by month 12 (~74%) and substantial by month 24 (~58%), every step justified by the ledger rather than by a vendor claim.
